origin.ja: 尾張の人。はじめ[[p:織田信長]]の弟の信勝 (信行) に仕え、稲生の戦いで信長に敗れたのち、信長に仕えて重く用いられた。
origin.en: A man of Owari. He first served [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]]'s brother Nobukatsu (Nobuyuki); beaten by Nobunaga at Ino, he went over to him and rose high.

origin.ja: 尾張の丹羽長政の子。若いころから[[p:織田信長]]に仕え、信長の兄信広の娘 (信長の養女) を妻とした。「米五郎左」と呼ばれたと伝わる。
origin.en: Son of Niwa Nagamasa of Owari. He served [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]] from his youth and married a daughter of Nobunaga's brother Nobuhiro (adopted by Nobunaga). He is said to have been called "Gorōza the rice".

origin.ja: 近江甲賀の出と伝わる。鉄砲の扱いに長け、信長に仕えて伊勢攻めで功を立てた。
origin.en: Said to come from Kōka in Ōmi. Skilled with the gun, he served Nobunaga and made his name in the conquest of Ise.

origin.ja: 尾張の佐久間氏の人。信長の父信秀の代から織田家に仕え、若いころの信長を支えた古参の重臣。
origin.en: Of the Sakuma of Owari. He served the Oda from Nobunaga's father Nobuhide's day, and was a senior retainer at the young Nobunaga's side.

origin.ja: 美濃の人。斎藤道三に仕えたのち信長に仕えた。子に森長可・森蘭丸がいる。
origin.en: A man of Mino. He served Saitō Dōsan, then Nobunaga. His sons included Mori Nagayoshi and Mori Ranmaru.

origin.ja: 尾張荒子の前田利春の四男。少年のころから信長の小姓として仕え、槍の名手で「槍の又左」と呼ばれた。
origin.en: Fourth son of Maeda Toshiharu of Arako in Owari. A page of Nobunaga from boyhood and a master of the spear — "Matazaemon of the spear".

origin.ja: 母が信長の乳母で、信長とは乳兄弟。
origin.en: His mother was Nobunaga's wet nurse: he and Nobunaga were milk brothers.

origin.ja: 美濃の土豪竹中重元の子 (名は重治)。[[p:斎藤龍興]]に仕えていた1564年、わずかな手勢で主君の稲葉山城を奪い、のちに返した。のちに織田家に移り、[[p:羽柴秀吉]]の与力となった。
origin.en: Son of Takenaka Shigemoto, a country squire of Mino (his name was Shigeharu). Serving [[p:斎藤龍興|Saitō Tatsuoki]] in 1564, he seized his lord's castle of Inabayama with a handful of men, and later gave it back. He went over to the Oda and was attached to [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hashiba Hideyoshi]].

origin.ja: 美濃の土岐氏の流れをくむ明智氏の出とされるが、前半生ははっきりしない。越前の朝倉氏のもとにいたのち、[[p:足利義昭]]と信長を結ぶ役を務めて信長に仕えた。
origin.en: Said to be of the Akechi, a branch of the Toki of Mino, though his early life is obscure. After a time with the Asakura of Echizen he served as go-between for [[p:足利義昭|Ashikaga Yoshiaki]] and Nobunaga, and entered Nobunaga's service.

origin.ja: [[p:羽柴秀吉]]の弟 (父を同じくするとも異にするともいわれる)。尾張中村の百姓の家に生まれ、兄に従って織田家に仕えた。
origin.en: Younger brother of [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hashiba Hideyoshi]] (whether by the same father or not is disputed). Born to a farming family at Nakamura in Owari, he followed his brother into the Oda service.

origin.ja: 尾張蜂須賀郷の土豪で、小六の名で知られる。[[p:羽柴秀吉]]の初めからの家臣。
origin.en: A country squire of Hachisuka in Owari, known as Koroku; one of [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hashiba Hideyoshi]]'s first retainers.

origin.ja: 播磨姫路の黒田職隆の子。父とともに御着の小寺氏に仕え、主家を織田方につけて[[p:羽柴秀吉]]の播磨攻めを助けた。キリシタンでもあった。
origin.en: Son of Kuroda Mototaka of Himeji in Harima. With his father he served the Kodera of Gochaku, brought them over to the Oda, and helped [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hideyoshi]] take Harima. He was also a Christian.

origin.ja: 出自ははっきりしないが、摂津五百住の土豪の出とする説が有力。[[p:三好長慶]]の側近 (右筆とも) から身を起こし、大和を任されるまでになった。
origin.en: His origins are unclear, but most now think he came of a country family of Yosumi in Settsu. He rose from being a close aide (some say scribe) of [[p:三好長慶|Miyoshi Nagayoshi]] to be given charge of Yamato.

origin.ja: 幕臣三淵晴員の次男で、細川家の養子となった。将軍[[p:足利義輝]]に仕え、義輝の死後は[[p:足利義昭]]を奉じて信長と結んだ。和歌と古典の学に通じた。
origin.en: Second son of the shogun's retainer Mitsubuchi Harukazu, adopted into the Hosokawa. He served the shogun [[p:足利義輝|Ashikaga Yoshiteru]], and after his death backed [[p:足利義昭|Ashikaga Yoshiaki]] and joined with Nobunaga. He was learned in poetry and the classics.

origin.ja: 織田信秀の娘で、[[p:織田信長]]の妹。[[p:浅井長政]]に嫁いで三人の娘 ([[p:淀殿]]・初・[[p:江]]) を産み、のちに[[p:柴田勝家]]の妻となった。
origin.en: Daughter of Oda Nobuhide and sister of [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]]. Married to [[p:浅井長政|Azai Nagamasa]], she bore three daughters ([[p:淀殿|Chacha]], Hatsu and [[p:江|Gō]]); later she became the wife of [[p:柴田勝家|Shibata Katsuie]].

origin.ja: 堺の商人田中与兵衛の子で、名は与四郎。祖父の千阿弥にちなんで千を名のったと伝わる。茶の湯を北向道陳・武野紹鷗に学んだという。
origin.en: Son of Tanaka Yohyōe, a merchant of Sakai; his name was Yoshirō. He is said to have taken the name Sen from his grandfather Sen'ami, and to have learned tea from Kitamuki Dōchin and Takeno Jōō.

origin.ja: 近江の出と伝わり、堺に出て商いで財をなした。茶人武野紹鷗の娘婿となり、1568年の信長上洛の際に名物の壺「松島」と茶入「紹鷗茄子」を献じた。
origin.en: Said to come from Ōmi, he made his fortune trading in Sakai. Son-in-law of the tea master Takeno Jōō, he presented Nobunaga with the famous jar "Matsushima" and the tea caddy "Jōō Nasu" when Nobunaga entered Kyoto in 1568.

origin.ja: 志摩の水軍の家の出。北畠氏の後ろ盾を得た志摩の地頭衆に所領を追われたが、信長に仕えて志摩を取り戻した。
origin.en: Of a family of sea lords in Shima. Driven out by the other Shima lords, who had Kitabatake backing, he served Nobunaga and won Shima back.

origin.ja: 摂津の池田氏の家臣から身を起こし、主家をしのいで摂津を治めた。
origin.en: He rose from a retainer of the Ikeda of Settsu to outstrip his lords and rule Settsu.

origin.ja: [[p:織田信長]]の嫡男。
origin.en: Eldest son and heir of [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]].

origin.ja: 尾張の生まれ。若いころは寺にいたと伝わる。柴田勝家に仕えたのち弓の腕で[[p:織田信長]]の弓衆となり、のちに信長の一代を記した『信長公記』を著した。
origin.en: Born in Owari; said to have spent his youth in a temple. He served Shibata Katsuie, then joined [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]]'s archers for his skill with the bow, and later wrote the Shinchō kōki, the record of Nobunaga's life.

origin.ja: 京の絵師の家狩野家の人で、狩野松栄の長男、狩野元信の孫。祖父に絵を学び、信長の安土城の障壁画を描いた。
origin.en: Of the Kanō, a family of painters in Kyoto: eldest son of Kanō Shōei and grandson of Kanō Motonobu. Taught by his grandfather, he painted the walls of Nobunaga's Azuchi castle.

origin.ja: 能登七尾の武士奥村氏の生まれで、染物屋長谷川家の養子となった。能登で仏画を描いたのち、三十代で京に上った。
origin.en: Born to the Okumura, a warrior family of Nanao in Noto, and adopted by the Hasegawa, a family of dyers. He painted Buddhist pictures in Noto, then went up to Kyoto in his thirties.

origin.ja: [[p:明智光秀]]の娘で、名は玉 (珠)。信長のすすめで[[p:細川藤孝]]の子忠興に嫁いだ。のちにキリシタンとなり、ガラシャの名を受けた。
origin.en: Daughter of [[p:明智光秀|Akechi Mitsuhide]]; her name was Tama. At Nobunaga's urging she married Tadaoki, son of [[p:細川藤孝|Hosokawa Fujitaka]]. She later became a Christian and took the name Gracia.

origin.ja: 近江坂田郡石田村の土豪石田正継の次男。長浜城主となった[[p:羽柴秀吉]]に若くして仕えた。寺で茶を三度出して秀吉に見込まれたという話は、のちの書物に見える。
origin.en: Second son of Ishida Masatsugu, a country squire of Ishida in Sakata, Ōmi. He entered the service of [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hideyoshi]] young, when Hideyoshi became lord of Nagahama. The tale that he won Hideyoshi over by serving him tea three times at a temple appears only in later books.

origin.ja: 近江の出とされる (豊後とする説もある)。[[p:羽柴秀吉]]の小姓から仕えた。
origin.en: Said to come from Ōmi (some say Bungo). He served [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hideyoshi]] from a page.

origin.ja: 堺の薬種商小西隆佐の子。宇喜多直家に仕えたのち[[p:羽柴秀吉]]に仕えた。キリシタン。
origin.en: Son of Konishi Ryūsa, a Sakai apothecary-merchant. He served Ukita Naoie and then [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hideyoshi]]. A Christian.

origin.ja: 尾張中村の生まれ。母が[[p:羽柴秀吉]]の母の縁者で、幼くして秀吉に仕えた。賤ヶ岳の七本槍の一人。
origin.en: Born at Nakamura in Owari; his mother was related to [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hideyoshi]]'s mother, and he served Hideyoshi from childhood. One of the Seven Spears of Shizugatake.

origin.ja: 尾張の桶屋の子と伝わる。母が[[p:羽柴秀吉]]の叔母とされ、幼くして秀吉に仕えた。賤ヶ岳の七本槍の一人。
origin.en: Said to be the son of a cooper in Owari; his mother is said to have been [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hideyoshi]]'s aunt, and he served Hideyoshi from childhood. One of the Seven Spears of Shizugatake.

origin.ja: 秀吉の正室おね (北政所) の兄木下家定の子。秀吉の養子となり、のちに小早川隆景の養子となった。
origin.en: Son of Kinoshita Iesada, brother of Hideyoshi's wife Nene. Adopted by Hideyoshi, then by Kobayakawa Takakage.

origin.ja: [[p:真田昌幸]]の次男。若いころは上杉・豊臣のもとで人質として過ごした。
origin.en: Second son of [[p:真田昌幸|Sanada Masayuki]]; in his youth he lived as a hostage with the Uesugi and the Toyotomi.

origin.ja: [[p:浅井長政]]と[[p:お市]]の長女で、名は茶々。小谷城と北ノ庄城の落城で父母を失い、のちに[[p:羽柴秀吉]]の側室となって[[p:豊臣秀頼]]を産んだ。
origin.en: Eldest daughter of [[p:浅井長政|Azai Nagamasa]] and [[p:お市|Oichi]]; her name was Chacha. She lost her father at the fall of Odani and her mother at the fall of Kitanoshō, then became [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hideyoshi]]'s consort and bore [[p:豊臣秀頼|Toyotomi Hideyori]].

origin.ja: 三河の酒井氏の人。家康の父広忠の代から仕え、家康の叔母を妻とした、徳川の最古参。
origin.en: Of the Sakai of Mikawa. He served Ieyasu's father Hirotada and married Ieyasu's aunt — the senior of the Tokugawa veterans.

origin.ja: 三河の本多氏の人。代々松平家に仕えた家に生まれ、十三歳で初陣を飾った。
origin.en: Of the Honda of Mikawa, a family long in the service of the Matsudaira; he first went to war at thirteen.

origin.ja: 三河上野の榊原氏の人。少年のころ家康の小姓となった。
origin.en: Of the Sakakibara of Ueno in Mikawa; he became Ieyasu's page as a boy.

origin.ja: 三河の石川氏の人で、石川康正の子。[[p:徳川家康]]が今川氏の人質だったころから近くに仕えたと伝わる。1585年、徳川家を出奔して[[p:羽柴秀吉]]のもとに走った。
origin.en: Of the Ishikawa of Mikawa, son of Ishikawa Yasumasa. He is said to have served [[p:徳川家康|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] from the days when Ieyasu was a hostage of the Imagawa. In 1585 he fled the Tokugawa and went over to [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hideyoshi]].

origin.ja: 三河の本多氏の人で、本多俊正の子。鷹匠として[[p:徳川家康]]に仕えたと伝わる。1563年の三河の一揆で寺方について家康に背き、諸国を流れたのちに帰参した。
origin.en: Of the Honda of Mikawa, son of Honda Toshimasa. He is said to have served [[p:徳川家康|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] as a falconer. In the Mikawa rising of 1563 he sided with the temples against Ieyasu, wandered the provinces, and later came back.

origin.ja: 伊賀の服部氏の出。父の保長が伊賀を出て松平家に仕え、半蔵は三河で生まれた。
origin.en: Of the Hattori of Iga. His father Yasunaga left Iga to serve the Matsudaira, and Hanzō was born in Mikawa.

origin.ja: 遠江井伊谷の井伊氏の人。父が今川氏に殺され、寺にかくまわれて育ったのち、十五歳で家康に仕えた。
origin.en: Of the Ii of Iinoya in Tōtōmi. His father was killed by the Imagawa; hidden in temples as a boy, he entered Ieyasu's service at fifteen.

origin.ja: [[p:徳川家康]]の三男。
origin.en: Third son of [[p:徳川家康|Tokugawa Ieyasu]].

origin.ja: 陸奥会津の生まれで、蘆名氏の一族と伝わるが、前半生ははっきりしない。諸国の寺で学んだ僧で、晩年の[[p:徳川家康]]に重く用いられた。
origin.en: Said to be born in Aizu in Mutsu, of a branch of the Ashina, though his early life is obscure. A monk who studied at temples in many provinces, he was much trusted by [[p:徳川家康|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] in Ieyasu's last years.

origin.ja: 三河牛窪の出で、諸国を巡ったのち武田晴信に仕えたと『甲陽軍鑑』は伝える。「山本菅助」の名を記した書状も見つかっている (軍鑑の勘助と同じ人かは議論がある)。
origin.en: The Kōyō gunkan says he came from Ushikubo in Mikawa and served Takeda Harunobu after wandering the provinces. A letter naming a "Yamamoto Kansuke" has been found (whether he is the gunkan's Kansuke is still debated).

origin.ja: 武田信虎の子で、信玄の弟。父に愛されて跡継ぎにと望まれたと伝わるが、兄を立てて支え続けた。
origin.en: Son of Takeda Nobutora and younger brother of Shingen. His father is said to have wanted him as heir, but he stood by his brother to the end.

origin.ja: 甲斐の教来石氏の出。信玄に取り立てられて馬場の名跡を継いだ。
origin.en: Born a Kyōraishi of Kai; raised up by Shingen, he took on the name of the Baba.

origin.ja: 飯富虎昌の弟 (甥とも)。兄が謀反の罪で死ぬと、山県の名跡を継いだ。兄の赤備えを受け継いだ。
origin.en: Younger brother (or nephew) of Obu Toramasa. When his brother died for treason he took the name of the Yamagata, and inherited his red-armoured troop.

origin.ja: 甲斐石和の百姓の出と伝わる。少年のころ信玄の近習となって取り立てられた。『甲陽軍鑑』の元は彼の語りとされる。
origin.en: Said to be a farmer's son from Isawa in Kai, taken up as Shingen's attendant as a boy. The Kōyō gunkan is said to rest on his telling.

origin.ja: 信濃小県の海野氏の流れをくむ真田氏の人。武田・村上・諏訪の連合に故郷を追われて上野に逃れたが、のちに信玄に仕えて旧領を取り戻した。
origin.en: Of the Sanada, an offshoot of the Unno of Chiisagata in Shinano. Driven from home by the Takeda, Murakami and Suwa, he fled to Kōzuke, then served Shingen and won his lands back.

origin.ja: [[p:真田幸隆]]の三男。幼くして信玄の近習となり武藤家を継いだが、兄二人が長篠で戦死したため真田家を継いだ。
origin.en: Third son of [[p:真田幸隆|Sanada Yukitaka]]. A boy attendant of Shingen, he was adopted into the Mutō, but took over the Sanada when both his elder brothers fell at Nagashino.

origin.ja: 越後柿崎の国人。上杉謙信のもとで先陣を務めた。
origin.en: A local lord of Kakizaki in Echigo who led the vanguard for Uesugi Kenshin.

origin.ja: 越後上田の樋口兼豊の子。幼くして[[p:上杉景勝]]に仕え、1581年に直江信綱が殺されると、その妻お船の婿となって直江家を継いだ。
origin.en: Son of Higuchi Kanetoyo of Ueda in Echigo. He served [[p:上杉景勝|Uesugi Kagekatsu]] from boyhood, and when Naoe Nobutsuna was killed in 1581 he married his widow Osen and took over the Naoe.

origin.ja: 今川家臣の福島氏の出とされる。父の戦死後に北条氏綱に引き取られ、娘婿となって北条の名を与えられた。
origin.en: Said to be born a Kushima, of an Imagawa retainer family. After his father fell, Hōjō Ujitsuna took him in, married him to his daughter and gave him the Hōjō name.

origin.ja: [[p:毛利元就]]の三男。安芸の竹原小早川家の養子となり、のちに本家の沼田小早川家も継いだ。兄の[[p:吉川元春]]とともに毛利家を支えた。
origin.en: Third son of [[p:毛利元就|Mōri Motonari]]. Adopted into the Takehara Kobayakawa of Aki, he later took over the main Nuta Kobayakawa line as well, and with his brother [[p:吉川元春|Kikkawa Motoharu]] held up the Mōri.

origin.ja: 毛利元就の次男。母の実家の吉川家を継いだ。
origin.en: Second son of Mōri Motonari; he took over the Kikkawa, his mother's family.

origin.ja: 安芸の守護家武田氏の生まれとされる。家が滅びたのち寺に入って僧となり、毛利家の使僧として外交を担った。1573年の書状で信長の行く末と秀吉の出世を言い当てたことで知られる。
origin.en: Said to be born of the Takeda, the governors of Aki. When his house fell he entered a temple as a monk, and became the Mōri's envoy-monk. He is known for a letter of 1573 that foretold Nobunaga's fall and Hideyoshi's rise.

origin.ja: 瀬戸内の能島村上氏の当主。海の関を押さえて通る船から帆別銭を取った。
origin.en: Head of the Murakami of Noshima in the Inland Sea, who held the sea lanes and took toll from passing ships.

origin.ja: 出雲の尼子家臣山中氏の人。主家の再興を誓い、三日月に「願わくは我に七難八苦を与えたまえ」と祈ったと伝わる。
origin.en: Of the Yamanaka, retainers of the Amago of Izumo. Vowing to restore his lords, he prayed to the crescent moon, they say: "Grant me seven hardships and eight sufferings."

origin.ja: 宇喜多直家の子。父の死後に[[p:羽柴秀吉]]の猶子となり、秀吉の養女豪姫 (前田利家の娘) を妻とした。
origin.en: Son of Ukita Naoie. After his father's death he became [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hideyoshi]]'s ward and married Hideyoshi's adopted daughter Gō, a daughter of Maeda Toshiie.

origin.ja: 長宗我部元親の嫡男。名の「信」の字は織田信長から与えられた。
origin.en: Eldest son and heir of Chōsokabe Motochika; the "Nobu" of his name was granted by Oda Nobunaga.

origin.ja: 豊後の大友一族の戸次氏の出 (戸次鑑連)。若いころ雷に打たれて足が不自由になったと伝わり、輿に乗って戦場に出た。
origin.en: Born a Bekki, a branch of the Ōtomo of Bungo (Bekki Akitsura). Struck by lightning as a young man, they say, he was lamed, and went to war carried in a litter.

origin.ja: 大友家臣吉弘鑑理の子で、高橋家を継いだ。[[p:立花宗茂]]の実の父。
origin.en: Son of the Ōtomo retainer Yoshihiro Akimasa; he took over the Takahashi. Father of [[p:立花宗茂|Tachibana Muneshige]].

origin.ja: [[p:高橋紹運]]の子。[[p:立花道雪]]に望まれてその一人娘誾千代の婿となり、立花家を継いだ。
origin.en: Son of [[p:高橋紹運|Takahashi Jōun]]. [[p:立花道雪|Tachibana Dōsetsu]] asked for him as husband for his only daughter Ginchiyo, and he became heir to the Tachibana.

origin.ja: 島津貴久の次男。兄義久を助け、九州の戦いの多くで先頭に立った。
origin.en: Second son of Shimazu Takahisa; he backed his brother Yoshihisa and led in most of the Kyushu wars.

origin.ja: 島津貴久の三男。祖父忠良に「始終の利害を察する智計並びなし」と評された。
origin.en: Third son of Shimazu Takahisa, praised by his grandfather Tadayoshi as unequalled at weighing gain and loss from first to last.

origin.ja: 島津貴久の四男。祖父忠良に「軍法戦術に妙を得たり」と評された。
origin.en: Fourth son of Shimazu Takahisa, praised by his grandfather Tadayoshi as a master of tactics.

origin.ja: 肥前佐嘉の鍋島清房の次男。母は龍造寺氏の娘で、のちに父が[[p:龍造寺隆信]]の母を後妻に迎えたため、隆信の義弟となった。
origin.en: Second son of Nabeshima Kiyofusa of Saga in Hizen. His mother was a Ryūzōji, and when his father later married [[p:龍造寺隆信|Ryūzōji Takanobu]]'s mother he became Takanobu's stepbrother.

origin.ja: 出羽米沢の八幡社の神職片倉景重の子。異父姉の喜多が[[p:伊達政宗]]の乳母を務めた縁で、少年の政宗の守り役となった。
origin.en: Son of Katakura Kageshige, a priest of the Hachiman shrine at Yonezawa in Dewa. His half-sister Kita was [[p:伊達政宗|Date Masamune]]'s nurse, and through her he became the boy Masamune's guardian.

origin.ja: 伊達一門の伊達実元の子。[[p:伊達政宗]]とは一つ違いで、幼いころから政宗に従った。
origin.en: Son of Date Sanemoto, of the Date family; a year apart from [[p:伊達政宗|Date Masamune]], he followed him from boyhood.

origin.ja: 伊達家臣山口常成の子で、伯父支倉時正の養子となった。1613年、[[p:伊達政宗]]の使節としてメキシコ・スペインを経てローマへ渡った。
origin.en: Son of the Date retainer Yamaguchi Tsunenari, adopted by his uncle Hasekura Tokimasa. In 1613 he sailed as [[p:伊達政宗|Date Masamune]]'s envoy by way of Mexico and Spain to Rome.

origin.ja: 本願寺の坊官を代々務めた下間氏の人。
origin.en: Of the Shimozuma, who served the Honganji as its stewards generation after generation.

origin.ja: 紀伊雑賀の鈴木氏の人で、鉄砲を操る雑賀衆の頭目の一人。「雑賀孫市」の名で知られる。
origin.en: Of the Suzuki of Saika in Kii, one of the leaders of the gun-wielding Saika band — known as Saika Magoichi.

origin.ja: ポルトガルのリスボンの生まれ。十代で修道会に入ってインドのゴアに渡り、1563年に宣教師として日本に来た。[[p:織田信長]]にたびたび会い、日本での布教の歴史を書き残した。
origin.en: Born in Lisbon, Portugal. He joined a religious order in his teens, went to Goa in India, and came to Japan as a missionary in 1563. He met [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]] many times and wrote a history of the mission in Japan.

origin.ja: ナポリ王国キエーティの貴族の家の生まれ。パドヴァで法学を学んだのち修道会に入り、東洋の巡察師として1579年に来日した。日本の少年たちを使節としてローマへ送り出した。
origin.en: Born to a noble family of Chieti in the Kingdom of Naples. He studied law at Padua, joined a religious order, and came to Japan in 1579 as its visitor to the East. He sent a party of Japanese boys to Rome as envoys.

origin.ja: 出雲大社の巫女と名のって諸国を巡ったと伝わるが、生い立ちは確かではない。京でかぶき踊りを演じて評判をとった。
origin.en: She is said to have toured the provinces calling herself a shrine maiden of Izumo, but her early life is uncertain. Her kabuki dancing in Kyoto made her famous.

origin.ja: 自著で播磨の生まれと記す (美作とする説もある)。十三歳で初めて勝負して勝ち、以後六十余度の勝負に一度も負けなかったと自ら書き残した。
origin.en: In his own book he says he was born in Harima (some say Mimasaka). He wrote that he fought his first duel at thirteen and won, and never lost in more than sixty bouts after.

origin.ja: 奈多八幡の社家奈多氏の出で、大友氏の一族田原氏を継いだ。大友宗麟の妻と同じ家の出。
origin.en: Born a Nata, of the priestly house of Nata Hachiman (the family of Ōtomo Sōrin's wife); he was adopted into the Tawara, a branch of the Ōtomo.

origin.ja: 豊後の大友氏の一族田北氏の人。
origin.en: Of the Tagita, a branch of the Ōtomo of Bungo.

origin.ja: 摂津高山の出。父の友照とともに少年のころキリシタンとなった。
origin.en: From Takayama in Settsu; with his father Tomoteru he became a Christian as a boy.

origin.ja: 播磨の出。黒田孝高 (官兵衛) に育てられ、黒田長政に仕えたが、のちに黒田家を出た。
origin.en: From Harima. Raised by Kuroda Yoshitaka (Kanbei), he served Kuroda Nagamasa, and later left the Kuroda.

origin.ja: 近江日野の蒲生賢秀の子。人質として信長のもとに送られたが、才を見込まれて信長の娘を妻に迎えた。
origin.en: Son of Gamō Katahide of Hino in Ōmi. Sent to Nobunaga as a hostage, he so impressed him that Nobunaga gave him his daughter in marriage.

origin.ja: 確かな記録は乏しく、「佐々木小次郎」の名も後世の書物に見える。越前の出で富田流の剣を学んだとも伝わる。「岩流」と呼ばれ、舟島で[[p:宮本武蔵]]と戦ったとされる。
origin.en: Little reliable is known; even the name Sasaki Kojirō first appears in later books, which say he came from Echizen and learned the Toda style of swordsmanship. Known as "Ganryū", he is said to have fought [[p:宮本武蔵|Miyamoto Musashi]] on Funashima.

origin.ja: 美濃の斎藤道三の娘で、母は明智氏の出と伝わる。1549年、尾張との和睦のしるしに[[p:織田信長]]に嫁いだ。のちの消息ははっきりしない。
origin.en: Daughter of Saitō Dōsan of Mino; her mother is said to have been an Akechi. In 1549 she was married to [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]] to seal peace with Owari. What became of her later is unclear.

origin.ja: 尾張の杉原定利の娘で、叔母の嫁ぎ先の浅野長勝の養女となった。1561年、まだ身分の低かった[[p:羽柴秀吉]]に嫁いだ。
origin.en: Daughter of Sugihara Sadatoshi of Owari, adopted by Asano Nagakatsu, her aunt's husband. In 1561 she married [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hashiba Hideyoshi]], then still a man of low rank.

origin.ja: 今川家臣関口氏純 (親永) の娘で、母は[[p:今川義元]]の妹とも伝わる。今川氏の人質だった[[p:徳川家康]]に嫁ぎ、嫡男信康を産んだ。
origin.en: Daughter of the Imagawa retainer Sekiguchi Ujizumi (Chikanaga); her mother is said to have been a sister of [[p:今川義元|Imagawa Yoshimoto]]. She married [[p:徳川家康|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] while he was a hostage of the Imagawa, and bore his heir Nobuyasu.

origin.ja: 尾張の篠原一計の娘。母方の縁で[[p:前田利家]]の家に引き取られて育ち、十二歳で利家に嫁いだ。
origin.en: Daughter of Shinohara Kazutoshi of Owari. Through her mother's family she was taken in and raised in the house of [[p:前田利家|Maeda Toshiie]], and married him at twelve.

origin.ja: [[p:浅井長政]]と[[p:お市]]の三女で、[[p:淀殿]]の妹。三度嫁ぎ、三度目に[[p:徳川秀忠]]の妻となって[[p:千姫]]や家光を産んだ。
origin.en: Third daughter of [[p:浅井長政|Azai Nagamasa]] and [[p:お市|Oichi]], sister of [[p:淀殿|Lady Yodo]]. Married three times, the third time to [[p:徳川秀忠|Tokugawa Hidetada]], she bore [[p:千姫|Lady Sen]] and Iemitsu.

origin.ja: [[p:徳川秀忠]]と[[p:江]]の長女。七歳で[[p:豊臣秀頼]]に嫁ぎ、1615年の大坂城落城の際に城から救い出された。
origin.en: Eldest daughter of [[p:徳川秀忠|Tokugawa Hidetada]] and [[p:江|Gō]]. Married to [[p:豊臣秀頼|Toyotomi Hideyori]] at seven, she was brought out of Osaka castle when it fell in 1615.

origin.ja: 陸奥三春の田村清顕の一人娘で、母は相馬氏の出。十二歳で[[p:伊達政宗]]に嫁いだ。
origin.en: Only daughter of Tamura Kiyoaki of Miharu in Mutsu; her mother was a Sōma. She married [[p:伊達政宗|Date Masamune]] at twelve.

events.ja: 桶狭間の戦い。二万を超える軍で尾張へ攻め入った[[p:今川義元]]を、{r_oda}はわずかな兵で急襲し、豪雨の中で討ち取った。
events.en: The battle of Okehazama. [[p:今川義元|Imagawa Yoshimoto]] invaded Owari with over twenty thousand men; {r_oda} fell on him with a few thousand in a downpour and took his head.

events.ja: 今川家の人質として育った{r_tokugawa}は、桶狭間の後に岡崎城へ戻り、今川から自立した。
events.en: Raised a hostage of the Imagawa, {r_tokugawa} returned to Okazaki after Okehazama and broke free of them.

events.ja: 長尾景虎は関東管領上杉憲政から上杉の名跡と管領職を譲られ、鶴岡八幡宮で拝賀した。以後、{n_uesugi}は上杉家を名乗る。
events.en: Nagao Kagetora received the Uesugi name and the office of Kantō deputy from Uesugi Norimasa, and gave thanks at the Tsurugaoka shrine. The house now called itself Uesugi.

events.ja: 第四次川中島の戦い。霧の八幡原で{n_takeda}と{n_uesugi}が激突した。謙信が単騎で信玄の本陣に斬り込み、信玄が軍配で受けたとも伝わる。[[p:武田信繁]]・[[p:山本勘助]]が討死し、両軍とも多くを失った。
events.en: The fourth battle of Kawanakajima. {n_takeda} and {n_uesugi} clashed in the fog of Hachimanbara; legend has Kenshin riding alone into Shingen's camp and Shingen parrying with his war fan. [[p:武田信繁|Takeda Nobushige]] and [[p:山本勘助|Yamamoto Kansuke]] fell, and both armies bled.

events.ja: 清洲同盟。{r_oda}と{r_tokugawa}は盟を結び、互いの背を預けた。この同盟は二十年続く。
events.en: The Kiyosu alliance. {r_oda} and {r_tokugawa} swore to guard each other's backs; the bond would hold for twenty years.

events.ja: {r_omura}は宣教師から[[a:kirisuto|洗礼を受け]]、最初のキリシタン大名となった。南蛮船は{n_omura}の港に入るようになった。
events.en: {r_omura} was [[a:kirisuto|baptised]] by the missionaries, the first Christian daimyo. The southern barbarian ships began to call at the ports of {n_omura}.

events.ja: 三河で門徒衆が蜂起し、{n_tokugawa}の家臣にも主君に背く者が出た。{r_tokugawa}は半年かけてこれを鎮めた。
events.en: The believers of Mikawa rose, and some of {n_tokugawa}'s own retainers turned against their lord. {r_tokugawa} needed half a year to put it down.

events.ja: [[p:竹中半兵衛]]は舅の安藤守就とともに、わずか十数人で稲葉山城を乗っ取り、{r_saito}を城から追った。半年ほどのちに城を龍興に返し、自らは隠棲した。
events.en: [[p:竹中半兵衛|Takenaka Hanbei]] and his father-in-law Andō Morinari seized Inabayama castle with barely a dozen men and drove {r_saito} out. Half a year later Hanbei gave the castle back to Tatsuoki and retired.

events.ja: 永禄の変。三好の一党が京の御所を襲い、将軍[[p:足利義輝]]は自ら刀を取って戦ったのち討たれた。
events.en: The Eiroku incident. A Miyoshi faction stormed the shogun's palace in Kyoto; [[p:足利義輝|Ashikaga Yoshiteru]] fought with his own sword before he was cut down.

events.ja: {r_takeda}は上野の箕輪城を落とし、{n_nagano}を滅ぼした。
events.en: {r_takeda} took Minowa castle in Kōzuke and destroyed {n_nagano}.

events.ja: 松平家康は朝廷の許しを得て、姓を徳川と改めた。
events.en: With the court's leave, [[p:まつ|Matsu]]daira Ieyasu changed his family name to Tokugawa.

events.ja: 月山富田城が開城し、{n_amago}は{n_mori}に降った。[[p:毛利元就]]は中国地方の覇者となった。
events.en: Gassan-Toda castle opened its gates and {n_amago} submitted to {n_mori}. [[p:毛利元就|Mōri Motonari]] was master of the Chūgoku region.

events.ja: {r_oda}は稲葉山城を落として美濃を手に入れ、城下を岐阜と改めた。この頃から「天下布武」の印を用いはじめる。
events.en: {r_oda} took Inabayama and with it Mino, renamed the castle town Gifu, and began to use a seal reading "the realm under arms".

events.ja: {r_oda}は稲葉山を岐阜と改め、城下の加納に楽市の制札を掲げた。座の特権や市の税をなくし、誰もが自由に商いのできる市とした。この頃から「天下布武」の印を使い始める。
events.en: {r_oda} renamed Inabayama as Gifu and posted a free-market notice at Kanō below the castle: no guild privileges, no market dues, trade open to all. About this time he began to use the seal "the realm under arms".

events.ja: {r_oda}は[[p:足利義昭]]を奉じて上洛し、行く手を阻んだ{n_rokkaku}を観音寺城に破り、三好の軍を摂津から退けた。義昭は第十五代将軍となった。
events.en: {r_oda} marched on Kyoto as escort of [[p:足利義昭|Ashikaga Yoshiaki]], broke {n_rokkaku} at Kannonji and drove the Miyoshi out of Settsu. Yoshiaki became the fifteenth shogun.

events.ja: {r_takeda}は今川との同盟を破って駿河に攻め入り、駿府を落とした。[[p:今川氏真]]は掛川へ逃れた。
events.en: {r_takeda} broke the alliance with the Imagawa, invaded Suruga and took Sunpu; [[p:今川氏真|Imagawa Ujizane]] fled to Kakegawa.

events.ja: 掛川城が開城し、戦国大名としての{n_imagawa}は滅んだ。氏真は妻の実家の北条家に身を寄せ、のちに歌と蹴鞠に生きた。
events.en: Kakegawa opened its gates and {n_imagawa} was finished as a warlord house. Ujizane went to his wife's family, the Hōjō, and later lived for poetry and football.

events.ja: 三増峠の戦い。小田原城を囲んだのち甲斐へ引き揚げる{r_takeda}の軍を、北条勢が相模の三増峠で待ち受けた。信玄は別働隊を山の上に回り込ませ、北条勢を打ち破って帰国した。
events.en: The battle of Mimase pass. As {r_takeda} marched home to Kai after besieging Odawara, the Hōjō lay in wait at Mimase pass in Sagami; Shingen sent a detachment round onto the heights, broke them and went home.

events.ja: {r_oda}は伊勢の{n_kitabatake}を攻めて和を結ばせ、次男信雄を北畠の養子とした。
events.en: {r_oda} invaded Ise and forced {n_kitabatake} to terms, making his second son Nobukatsu the Kitabatake heir.

events.ja: {r_satake}は常陸の{n_oda_h}を攻め、小田城を奪った。
events.en: {r_satake} attacked {n_oda_h} in Hitachi and took Oda castle.

events.ja: {r_oda}は越前の{n_asakura}を攻めたが、妹[[p:お市]]の嫁ぎ先{n_azai}が背いて退路を断った。[[a:kanegasaki_nokiguchi|木下藤吉郎が殿を]]務め、信長はわずかな供と京へ逃れた (金ヶ崎の退き口)。
events.en: {r_oda} invaded {n_asakura} in Echizen, but {n_azai}, whose lord had married his sister [[p:お市|Oichi]], turned and cut the road home. [[a:kanegasaki_nokiguchi|Kinoshita Tōkichirō held the rear]] while Nobunaga fled to Kyoto with a handful of men.

events.ja: {r_tokugawa}は居城を岡崎から遠江の引間に移し、浜松と名を改めた。岡崎は嫡男の信康に任せた。
events.en: {r_tokugawa} moved his seat from Okazaki to Hikuma in Tōtōmi and renamed it Hamamatsu, leaving Okazaki to his heir Nobuyasu.

events.ja: 姉川の戦い。{n_oda}と{n_tokugawa}の軍が{n_azai}・{n_asakura}の軍を姉川の河原で破った。
events.en: The battle of the Ane river. The armies of {n_oda} and {n_tokugawa} defeated {n_azai} and {n_asakura} on its gravel banks.

events.ja: {r_ishiyama}は諸国の門徒に檄を飛ばし、{n_oda}との戦いに立った。石山合戦の始まりで、戦いは十年に及ぶ。
events.en: {r_ishiyama} called the believers of every province to arms against {n_oda}. So began the Ishiyama war, which would last ten years.

events.ja: 伊勢長島の門徒衆が蜂起し、{n_oda}の小木江城を攻め落とした。
events.en: The believers of Nagashima in Ise rose and took a castle of {n_oda}.

events.ja: 南部家の一族大浦為信が主家に背いて石川城を落とし、津軽の地を切り取りはじめた。
events.en: Ōura Tamenobu, a kinsman of the Nanbu, rose against his lords, took Ishikawa castle and began to carve out Tsugaru for himself.

events.ja: [[p:毛利元就]]は世を去った。三人の子に[[a:sanbon_ya|「一本の矢は折れても三本束ねれば折れぬ」]]と諭したという話は、後世の作り話ともいわれる。
events.en: [[p:毛利元就|Mōri Motonari]] died. The tale of his teaching his three sons that [[a:sanbon_ya|one arrow breaks but three together do not]] may be a later invention.

events.ja: 比叡山焼き討ち。浅井・朝倉に味方した比叡山の僧兵を{r_oda}は許さず、山上の堂塔を焼き払った。多くの人々が命を落とした。
events.en: The burning of Mount Hiei. {r_oda} would not forgive the warrior monks of Hiei for siding with Azai and Asakura, and burned the halls on the mountain. Many people lost their lives.

events.ja: 三方ヶ原の戦い。西上する{r_takeda}の大軍に{r_tokugawa}は挑んだが大敗し、浜松城へ逃げ帰った。家康はこの時の苦い顔を絵に描かせて戒めとしたと伝わる。
events.en: The battle of Mikatagahara. {r_tokugawa} challenged the great army of {r_takeda} marching west and was routed back to Hamamatsu. He is said to have had his grimace painted to remind himself.

events.ja: [[p:武田信玄]]は西上の途上で病に倒れ、甲斐へ戻る途中で世を去った。「三年はわが死を秘せよ」と遺言したという。
events.en: [[p:武田信玄|Takeda Shingen]] fell ill on the march west and died on the way home. He is said to have ordered his death kept secret for three years.

events.ja: {r_ashikaga}は{n_oda}に兵を挙げたが敗れ、京から追放された。二百四十年続いた室町幕府はここに事実上終わった。
events.en: {r_ashikaga} rose against {n_oda}, lost, and was driven from Kyoto. The Muromachi shogunate, two hundred and forty years old, was in effect at an end.

events.ja: {r_oda}は刀根坂で{n_asakura}を破って一乗谷を焼き、[[p:朝倉義景]]は自害した。
events.en: {r_oda} broke {n_asakura} at Tonezaka and burned Ichijōdani; [[p:朝倉義景|Asakura Yoshikage]] took his own life.

events.ja: 小谷城が落ち、[[p:浅井長政]]は自害した。[[p:お市]]と三人の娘は城から救い出された。
events.en: Odani fell and [[p:浅井長政|Azai Nagamasa]] took his own life. [[p:お市|Oichi]] and her three daughters were brought out of the castle.

events.ja: [[p:三好義継]]が若江城で討たれ、畿内の三好の地は{n_oda}の手に落ちた。三好の一族は阿波に拠って残った。
events.en: [[p:三好義継|Miyoshi Yoshitsugu]] fell at Wakae, and the Miyoshi lands of the capital region passed to {n_oda}; the family held on in Awa.

events.ja: {r_oda}は東大寺の正倉院に納められた名香「蘭奢待」を一寸八分切り取らせた。足利義政以来、百年ぶりのことであった。
events.en: {r_oda} had an inch and more cut from Ranjatai, the famous aloeswood kept in the Shōsōin of Tōdaiji — the first time since the shogun Yoshimasa, a hundred years before.

events.ja: 三度目の攻めで{r_oda}は長島を兵糧攻めにし、降った門徒衆までも討った。
events.en: In his third attempt {r_oda} starved Nagashima into surrender, and put even those who surrendered to the sword.

events.ja: 河内の高屋城が{n_oda}に降った。
events.en: Takaya castle in Kawachi surrendered to {n_oda}.

events.ja: 長篠の戦い。{n_oda}と{n_tokugawa}は馬防柵の内から多くの[[a:teppo|鉄砲]]を撃ちかけ、{n_takeda}の[[a:takeda_horse|騎馬隊]]を破った。[[p:山県昌景]]・[[p:馬場信春]]ら武田の名将の多くが討死した。
events.en: The battle of Nagashino. From behind palisades {n_oda} and {n_tokugawa} met the [[a:takeda_horse|horsemen]] of {n_takeda} with massed [[a:teppo|musket fire]]. [[p:山県昌景|Yamagata Masakage]], [[p:馬場信春|Baba Nobuharu]] and many of Takeda's best fell.

events.ja: 備中兵乱。{r_mori}は{n_mimura}を滅ぼし、備中を手に入れた。
events.en: The Bitchū war: {r_mori} destroyed {n_mimura} and took Bitchū.

events.ja: 四万十川の戦い。{r_chosokabe}は{n_ichijo}を破り、土佐を一つにした。
events.en: At the Shimanto river {r_chosokabe} defeated {n_ichijo} and united Tosa.

events.ja: 浦上家の重臣[[p:宇喜多直家]]は主家に背き、備前の大半を手に入れた。
events.en: [[p:宇喜多直家|Ukita Naoie]], chief retainer of the Urakami, turned on his lords and took most of Bizen.

events.ja: 天神山城が落ち、[[p:浦上宗景]]は播磨へ逃れた。
events.en: Tenjinyama fell, and [[p:浦上宗景|Urakami Munekage]] fled to Harima.

events.ja: {r_oda}は琵琶湖のほとりに[[a:azuchi_castle|安土城]]を築きはじめた。五層七重の天主は、宣教師たちを驚かせた。
events.en: {r_oda} began [[a:azuchi_castle|Azuchi castle]] by Lake Biwa. Its seven-storeyed keep astonished the missionaries.

events.ja: 第一次木津川口の戦い。{n_mori}の水軍が焙烙火矢で織田の船を焼き、石山に兵糧を運び込んだ。
events.en: The first battle of the Kizu river mouth. The Mōri fleet burned Oda's ships with fire pots and brought food into Ishiyama.

events.ja: {r_uesugi}は越中に攻め入り、{n_jinbo}の地を平らげた。
events.en: {r_uesugi} invaded Etchū and took the lands of {n_jinbo}.

events.ja: 三瀬の変。[[p:北畠具教]]は{n_oda}の手の者に討たれ、伊勢は織田のものとなった。
events.en: The Mise incident: [[p:北畠具教|Kitabatake Tomonori]] was killed by men of {n_oda}, and Ise became Oda land.

events.ja: {r_uesugi}は七尾城を落として能登を取り、援軍に来た[[p:柴田勝家]]の軍を手取川で破った。「聞くと見るとは大違い、案外弱い信長」と謙信は言ったと伝わる。
events.en: {r_uesugi} took Nanao and Noto, and beat [[p:柴田勝家|Shibata Katsuie]]'s relief army at the Tedori river. "Nobunaga is weaker than his name," Kenshin is said to have remarked.

events.ja: 信貴山城の戦い。二度目の謀反を起こした[[p:松永久秀]]は信貴山城に籠もったが、[[p:織田信忠]]の大軍に囲まれて城とともに果てた。名物の茶釜「平蜘蛛」を打ち砕いて死んだと伝わる。
events.en: The siege of Shigisan. [[p:松永久秀|Matsunaga Hisahide]], in revolt for the second time, shut himself in Shigisan castle; surrounded by [[p:織田信忠|Oda Nobutada]]'s great army, he died with it — smashing, the story goes, his famous tea kettle "Hiragumo" first.

events.ja: {n_ito}の[[p:伊東義祐]]は{n_shimazu}に追われ、豊後の大友を頼って落ちのびた。
events.en: [[p:伊東義祐|Itō Yoshisuke]] of {n_ito}, driven out by {n_shimazu}, fled to the Ōtomo in Bungo.

events.ja: [[p:上杉謙信]]は春日山城で急死した。跡継ぎを定めていなかったため、養子の景勝と景虎が家督を争った (御館の乱)。
events.en: [[p:上杉謙信|Uesugi Kenshin]] died suddenly at Kasugayama without naming an heir; his adopted sons Kagekatsu and Kagetora fought over the house.

events.ja: {r_otomo}は洗礼を受け、日向に理想のキリシタンの国を築こうと南へ兵を進めた。
events.en: {r_otomo} was baptised and marched south to found an ideal Christian land in Hyūga.

events.ja: 摂津有岡城の[[p:荒木村重]]が{r_oda}に背いた。説得に赴いた[[p:黒田官兵衛]]は城中に捕らえられ、一年近く土牢に閉じ込められた。
events.en: [[p:荒木村重|Araki Murashige]] of Arioka castle in Settsu turned against {r_oda}. [[p:黒田官兵衛|Kuroda Kanbei]], who went to talk him round, was seized and kept nearly a year in a dungeon.

events.ja: 耳川の戦い。{n_shimazu}は[[a:tsurinobuse|「釣り野伏せ」]]で{n_otomo}の大軍を誘い込んで破った。大友の勢いはこれより衰える。
events.en: The battle of the Mimi river. {n_shimazu} lured the great army of {n_otomo} into its "[[a:tsurinobuse|fishing ambush]]" and broke it; the Ōtomo never recovered.

events.ja: 第二次木津川口の戦い。[[p:九鬼嘉隆]]の鉄張りの大船が毛利の水軍を退けた。
events.en: The second battle of the Kizu river mouth. [[p:九鬼嘉隆|Kuki Yoshitaka]]'s iron-plated ships drove off the Mōri fleet.

events.ja: [[p:明智光秀]]は丹波の八上城を囲んで{n_hatano}を降し、丹波を平らげた。
events.en: [[p:明智光秀|Akechi Mitsuhide]] besieged Yakami and brought down {n_hatano}; Tanba was pacified.

events.ja: 丹後の{n_isshiki}は{n_oda}の[[p:細川藤孝]]に攻められて滅んだ。
events.en: {n_isshiki} of Tango fell to [[p:細川藤孝|Hosokawa Fujitaka]] of {n_oda}.

events.ja: 信長の疑いを受け、{r_tokugawa}は正室の[[p:築山殿]]を殺させ、嫡男の信康を二俣城で切腹させた。本当の理由は今もはっきりしない。
events.en: Under Nobunaga's suspicion, {r_tokugawa} had his wife [[p:築山殿|Lady Tsukiyama]] put to death and his heir Nobuyasu made to take his life at Futamata castle. The true reason is still unclear.

events.ja: 三木の干殺し。[[p:羽柴秀吉]]に二年近く囲まれた三木城は飢えに尽き、[[p:別所長治]]は城兵の命と引き換えに自害した。
events.en: The starving of Miki. Besieged by [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hashiba Hideyoshi]] for nearly two years, Miki ran out of food; [[p:別所長治|Bessho Nagaharu]] killed himself to spare his garrison.

events.ja: {r_arima}は洗礼を受けた。有馬の地にはセミナリオが開かれ、少年たちがラテン語と西洋の音楽を学んだ。
events.en: {r_arima} was baptised. A seminary opened in Arima, where boys learned Latin and Western music.

events.ja: [[p:羽柴秀長]]が但馬を攻め、{n_yamana}は降った。
events.en: [[p:羽柴秀長|Hashiba Hidenaga]] invaded Tajima, and {n_yamana} submitted.

events.ja: 朝廷の仲立ちで和が結ばれ、{r_ishiyama}は石山を退いて紀伊の鷺森へ移った。十年に及んだ石山合戦は終わった。
events.en: Through the court's mediation a peace was made; {r_ishiyama} left Ishiyama for Saginomori in Kii, and the ten-year war ended.

events.ja: [[p:柴田勝家]]は加賀の尾山御坊を落とし、百年近く門徒衆が治めた「百姓の持ちたる国」は終わった。
events.en: [[p:柴田勝家|Shibata Katsuie]] took the Oyama temple-fortress, and Kaga, for nearly a century "a province held by farmers" under its believers, came to an end.

events.ja: 京都御馬揃え。{r_oda}は正親町天皇の前で、着飾った武将たちの騎馬の行列を披露した。
events.en: The great horse parade in Kyoto: {r_oda} showed his finely dressed commanders on horseback before the emperor.

events.ja: 高天神城の戦い。{r_tokugawa}に一年半囲まれた遠江の高天神城は兵糧が尽き、城兵は打って出て全滅した。{r_takeda}は後詰めを送れず、武田を見限る者が増えていった。
events.en: The siege of Takatenjin. Starved out after a year and a half under {r_tokugawa}, the garrison of Takatenjin in Tōtōmi sallied and died to a man. {r_takeda} had sent no relief, and more and more men gave up on the Takeda.

events.ja: {n_oda}の[[p:柴田勝家]]・佐々成政らは能登と越中を上杉から奪った。
events.en: [[p:柴田勝家|Shibata Katsuie]] and Sassa Narimasa of {n_oda} took Noto and Etchū from the Uesugi.

events.ja: 天正伊賀の乱。{n_oda}の大軍が伊賀に攻め入り、{n_iga}は滅んだ。
events.en: The Tenshō Iga war. The great army of {n_oda} poured into Iga, and {n_iga} was destroyed.

events.ja: 鳥取の渇え殺し。[[p:羽柴秀吉]]は米を買い占めたうえで鳥取城を囲み、城は飢えて開城した。
events.en: The starving of Tottori. Hideyoshi bought up the rice of the region, then besieged Tottori until hunger opened its gates.

events.ja: 天正遣欧使節。大友・有馬・大村の名代として四人の少年が長崎を発ち、ローマへ向かった。
events.en: The Tenshō embassy: four boys sailed from Nagasaki for Rome as envoys of the Ōtomo, Arima and Ōmura.

events.ja: 甲州征伐。{n_oda}と{n_tokugawa}の軍が甲斐に攻め入ると、家臣たちは次々と寝返り、[[p:武田勝頼]]は天目山で自害した。名門武田家は滅んだ。
events.en: The conquest of Kai. As {n_oda} and {n_tokugawa} invaded, retainer after retainer went over; [[p:武田勝頼|Takeda Katsuyori]] killed himself at Tenmokuzan, and the great house of Takeda was no more.

events.ja: 武田攻めの功により、{r_oda}は駿河一国を{r_tokugawa}に与えた。家康は安土に礼に上り、信長は家康を手厚くもてなした。
events.en: For his part in the fall of the Takeda, {r_oda} gave all of Suruga to {r_tokugawa}. Ieyasu went up to Azuchi to give thanks, and Nobunaga entertained him lavishly.

events.ja: [[p:羽柴秀吉]]は備中高松城のまわりに堤を築いて水を引き入れ、城を湖に浮かべた。
events.en: Hideyoshi built a dyke round Takamatsu castle in Bitchū and let the rivers in, leaving the castle afloat in a lake.

events.ja: 本能寺の変。京の本能寺に泊まっていた[[p:織田信長]]を、中国へ向かうはずの[[p:明智光秀]]の軍が襲った。「是非に及ばず」と言って信長は自ら弓をとり、火の中で果てた。嫡男信忠も二条御所で討たれた。
events.en: The Honnōji incident. [[p:明智光秀|Akechi Mitsuhide]]'s army, bound for the west, turned on [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]] at the Honnōji temple in Kyoto. "It cannot be helped," Nobunaga said, took up a bow, and died in the flames; his heir Nobutada fell at Nijō.

events.ja: [[a:ogaeshi|中国大返し]]。[[p:羽柴秀吉]]は毛利と和を結んで十日で京へ駆け戻り、山崎の戦いで[[p:明智光秀]]を破った。光秀は落ちのびる途中で討たれた。
events.en: [[a:ogaeshi|The great return]]: Hideyoshi made peace with the Mōri, ran back to Kyoto in ten days, and beat [[p:明智光秀|Akechi Mitsuhide]] at Yamazaki; Mitsuhide was killed as he fled.

events.ja: 明智に味方した[[p:武田元明]]は自害させられ、若狭は{n_oda}の[[p:丹羽長秀]]の地となった。
events.en: [[p:武田元明|Takeda Motoaki]], who had sided with Akechi, was made to kill himself; Wakasa went to [[p:丹羽長秀|Niwa Nagahide]] of {n_oda}.

events.ja: 中富川の戦い。{r_chosokabe}は阿波の三好の残党を破り、勝瑞城を落とした。
events.en: At the Nakatomi river {r_chosokabe} beat the last of the Miyoshi in Awa and took Shōzui.

events.ja: 本能寺の変で主を失った旧武田領をめぐって、{r_tokugawa}・{r_hojo}・{r_uesugi}が争った (天正壬午の乱)。和議の末、甲斐と信濃の多くは徳川に、上野は北条に、北信濃は上杉に帰した。
events.en: With Nobunaga dead, {r_tokugawa}, {r_hojo} and {r_uesugi} fought over the old Takeda lands. At the peace most of Kai and Shinano went to Tokugawa, Kōzuke to Hōjō and northern Shinano to Uesugi.

events.ja: 賤ヶ岳の戦い。[[p:羽柴秀吉]]は[[p:柴田勝家]]を破り、勝家は[[p:お市]]とともに北ノ庄城で自害した。信長の後継者の座は秀吉のものとなった。
events.en: The battle of Shizugatake. Hideyoshi defeated [[p:柴田勝家|Shibata Katsuie]], who died with [[p:お市|Oichi]] in Kitanoshō castle. Nobunaga's place was Hideyoshi's.

events.ja: {r_oda}は石山の跡に[[a:osaka_castle|大坂城]]を築きはじめた。金箔の瓦をいただく天守が城下を見下ろした。
events.en: {r_oda} began [[a:osaka_castle|Osaka castle]] on the site of Ishiyama; a keep roofed with gold-leafed tiles looked down on the town.

events.ja: 小牧・長久手の戦い。{r_tokugawa}は織田信雄と組んで{n_oda}と戦い、長久手で別働隊を破ったが、秀吉は信雄と和を結んで家康の戦う理由を消した。
events.en: The Komaki-Nagakute campaign. {r_tokugawa}, allied with Oda Nobukatsu, fought {n_oda} and destroyed a flying column at Nagakute; but Hideyoshi made peace with Nobukatsu and left Ieyasu nothing to fight for.

events.ja: 沖田畷の戦い。有馬を攻めた{r_ryuzoji}の大軍は湿地の細道で{n_shimazu}と有馬の兵に囲まれ、隆信は討たれた。
events.en: The battle of Okitanawate. The great army of {r_ryuzoji}, marching on Arima, was caught on the causeways through the marsh by {n_shimazu} and the Arima; Takanobu was killed.

events.ja: {r_chosokabe}は伊予の{n_saionji}を降した。
events.en: {r_chosokabe} brought down {n_saionji} in Iyo.

events.ja: 紀州征伐。{r_oda}は根来寺を焼き、太田城を水攻めにして{n_saika}を降した。
events.en: The conquest of Kii. {r_oda} burned the Negoro temple, flooded Ōta castle and brought down {n_saika}.

events.ja: {r_oda}は関白に任じられた。農民の子から武家の頂点へ、前例のない出世であった。
events.en: {r_oda} was named regent (kanpaku): from a farmer's son to the summit of the warrior order, a rise without precedent.

events.ja: 四国平定。{n_oda}の大軍が四方から四国に渡り、{r_chosokabe}は土佐一国を安堵されて降った。
events.en: The conquest of Shikoku. The armies of {n_oda} crossed from every side, and {r_chosokabe} submitted, keeping Tosa alone.

events.ja: {r_shimazu}は肥後に兵を進め、{n_aso}を降した。
events.en: {r_shimazu} advanced into Higo and brought down {n_aso}.

events.ja: 伊予の{n_kono}は四国平定で滅び、伊予は[[p:小早川隆景]]に与えられた。
events.en: {n_kono} of Iyo fell in the conquest of Shikoku; Iyo was given to [[p:小早川隆景|Kobayakawa Takakage]].

events.ja: 金森長近が飛騨に攻め入り、{n_anegakoji}は滅んだ。
events.en: Kanamori Nagachika invaded Hida, and {n_anegakoji} fell.

events.ja: 人取橋の戦い。父輝宗の弔い合戦として二本松城を囲んだ{r_date}に、{r_satake}らの連合軍およそ三万が攻めかかった。伊達勢は人取橋で大きな損害を出し、老臣の鬼庭左月は討死したが、連合軍は夜のうちに兵を引いた。
events.en: The battle of Hitotoribashi. {r_date} was besieging Nihonmatsu to avenge his father Terumune when some thirty thousand allies under {r_satake} came at him. The Date lost heavily at the Hitotori bridge, where the old retainer Oniwa Sagetsu fell, but the allies withdrew in the night.

events.ja: {r_uesugi}は上洛して{r_oda}に臣従した。
events.en: {r_uesugi} came to the capital and submitted to {r_oda}.

events.ja: 父輝宗を死に追いやった二本松を{r_date}は攻め、二本松城を落とした。
events.en: {r_date} attacked Nihonmatsu, whose lord had caused his father Terumune's death, and took the castle.

events.ja: 岩屋城の戦い。筑前に攻め入った{n_shimazu}の大軍を、{n_otomo}の[[p:高橋紹運]]はわずか七百余りで半月にわたって防ぎ、城兵とともに果てた。島津は多くの兵と日数を失った。
events.en: The siege of Iwaya. [[p:高橋紹運|Takahashi Jōun]] of {n_otomo} held off the great {n_shimazu} army in Chikuzen for half a month with some seven hundred men, and died with all of them. The Shimazu lost many men and many days.

events.ja: {r_tokugawa}は大坂城に上って{r_oda}に臣下の礼をとった。
events.en: {r_tokugawa} went up to Osaka castle and knelt to {r_oda}.

events.ja: [[p:羽柴秀吉]]は朝廷から豊臣の姓を賜り、太政大臣となった。
events.en: [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hashiba Hideyoshi]] received the family name Toyotomi from the court and became chancellor of the realm.

events.ja: {r_tokugawa}は居城を浜松から駿府に移した。五か国を治めるには、駿府の方が中ほどにあった。
events.en: {r_tokugawa} moved his seat from Hamamatsu to Sunpu, nearer the middle of the five provinces he now ruled.

events.ja: 戸次川の戦い。豊後を救うため先に送られた{r_chosokabe}らの軍は、軍監の仙石秀久が押し切った渡河で{n_shimazu}の[[p:島津家久]]に破られた。元親の嫡男の信親は討死し、元親は力を落とした。
events.en: The battle of the Hetsugi river. The vanguard sent to save Bungo — {r_chosokabe} and others — was beaten by [[p:島津家久|Shimazu Iehisa]] of {n_shimazu} after the overseer Sengoku Hidehisa forced a river crossing. Motochika's heir Nobuchika was killed, and Motochika never recovered his spirit.

events.ja: 九州平定。二十万を超える{n_oda}の軍に、{r_shimazu}は剃髪して降った。九州の国々は秀吉の手で分け直された。
events.en: The conquest of Kyūshū. Before more than two hundred thousand men of {n_oda}, {r_shimazu} shaved his head and submitted. Kyūshū was parcelled out anew by Hideyoshi.

events.ja: 博多で秀吉はバテレン追放令を出し、宣教師に国外退去を命じた。ただし南蛮貿易は続けられ、命令は徹底されなかった。
events.en: At Hakata Hideyoshi issued the edict expelling the missionaries; but the trade with the southern barbarians went on and the edict was loosely kept.

events.ja: 十五里ヶ原の戦い。上杉の本庄繁長は庄内の{n_daihoji}を破り、庄内を取った。
events.en: At Jūgorigahara Honjō Shigenaga of the Uesugi beat {n_daihoji} and took Shōnai.

events.ja: [[a:katanagari|刀狩令]]。{r_oda}は百姓から刀・弓・鉄砲を取り上げ、武士と百姓の別を定めた。
events.en: [[a:katanagari|The sword hunt]]. {r_oda} took swords, bows and guns from the farmers, and fixed the line between warrior and farmer.

events.ja: 摺上原の戦い。{r_date}は{n_ashina}を破り、会津の黒川城に入った。南奥州の大半が伊達のものとなった。
events.en: The battle of Suriagehara. {r_date} defeated {n_ashina} and entered Kurokawa castle in Aizu; most of southern Ōu was Date land.

events.ja: 小田原征伐。二十万を超える軍に囲まれ、三か月の籠城ののち[[a:odawara_sogamae|小田原城]]は開いた。[[p:北条氏政]]は切腹し、五代百年の北条家は滅んだ。
events.en: The siege of [[a:odawara_sogamae|Odawara]]. Surrounded by more than two hundred thousand men, Odawara opened its gates after three months; [[p:北条氏政|Hōjō Ujimasa]] was made to kill himself, and the Hōjō, five generations and a century old, were gone.

events.ja: 北条に従った{n_chiba}は北条とともに滅び、その地は徳川の領となった。
events.en: {n_chiba}, having followed the Hōjō, fell with them; its land went to the Tokugawa.

events.ja: {r_tokugawa}は旧領の三河・遠江・駿河・甲斐・信濃を離れ、北条の旧領関東へ移された。家康は小田原ではなく、入江の寒村だった[[a:edo_castle|江戸]]を本拠に選んだ。
events.en: {r_tokugawa} was moved from his old lands to the Kantō of the fallen Hōjō. He chose for his seat not Odawara but [[a:edo_castle|Edo]], a poor village on an inlet.

events.ja: 奥州仕置。{r_oda}は奥羽の大名の領地を改め、遅れて小田原に参じた{r_date}から会津を取り上げた。天下は一つになった。
events.en: The settlement of the north. {r_oda} redrew the domains of Ōu and took Aizu from {r_date}, who had come late to Odawara. The realm was one.

events.ja: 北条に従った{n_yura}は所領を移された。
events.en: {n_yura}, having followed the Hōjō, was moved from its land.

events.ja: {n_yuki}は家康の次男秀康を養子に迎え、徳川の一門となった。
events.en: {n_yuki} adopted Ieyasu's second son Hideyasu and joined the Tokugawa family.

events.ja: {r_mori}は山間の吉田郡山を出て、太田川の河口の三角州に築いた広島城に入った。
events.en: {r_mori} left the hill castle of Yoshida-Kōriyama for Hiroshima, the new castle built on the delta at the mouth of the Ōta river.

events.ja: [[p:千利休]]は秀吉の怒りを買い、切腹を命じられた。その理由は今もはっきりしない。
events.en: [[p:千利休|Sen no Rikyū]] angered Hideyoshi and was ordered to take his own life; the reason is unclear to this day.

events.ja: 一揆を扇動した疑いをかけられた{r_date}は、米沢など先祖伝来の地を召し上げられ、一揆の跡の大崎・葛西の地に移されて岩出山に入った。
events.en: Suspected of stirring up the risings, {r_date} lost Yonezawa and his ancestral lands and was moved to the old Ōsaki and Kasai lands, taking up his seat at Iwadeyama.

events.ja: 九戸政実の乱。{r_nanbu}の一族、九戸政実が主家に背いて九戸城に籠もった。豊臣秀次を総大将とする奥州再仕置の大軍に囲まれ、命を助けるという約束で城を開いたが、政実は斬られた。
events.en: The rising of Kunohe Masazane. Masazane, a kinsman of {r_nanbu}, rose against his house and held Kunohe castle. Surrounded by the great army of the second settlement of the north under Toyotomi Hidetsugu, he opened the gates on a promise of his life, and was beheaded.

events.ja: 文禄の役。{r_oda}は朝鮮半島へ大軍を送った。各地で激しい戦いが続き、多くの人々が苦しんだ。
events.en: The Bunroku campaign. {r_oda} sent a great army across to the Korean peninsula; fierce fighting went on for years and great numbers of people suffered.

events.ja: 朝鮮の陣で敵を前に退いた[[p:大友義統]]は、秀吉に所領を取り上げられた。名門大友家は大名の座を失った。
events.en: [[p:大友義統|Ōtomo Yoshimune]], who had fallen back before the enemy in the Korean campaign, was stripped of his domain by Hideyoshi; the great house of Ōtomo was no longer a daimyo house.

events.ja: 大坂城で[[p:淀殿]]が男子を産んだ。幼名を拾といい、のちの[[p:豊臣秀頼]]である。{r_oda}は五十七歳であった。
events.en: At Osaka castle [[p:淀殿|Lady Yodo]] bore a son, called Hiroi as a child: the later [[p:豊臣秀頼|Toyotomi Hideyori]]. {r_oda} was fifty-seven.

events.ja: 秀次事件。謀反の疑いをかけられた関白の豊臣秀次は高野山に追われて切腹させられ、妻子三十余人も京の三条河原で斬られた。
events.en: The Hidetsugu affair. Accused of treason, the regent Toyotomi Hidetsugu was sent to Mount Kōya and made to take his life; more than thirty of his wives and children were beheaded at the Sanjō riverbed in Kyoto.

events.ja: 慶長伏見地震。京と畿内を大地震が襲い、できたばかりの伏見城の天守が崩れ、方広寺の大仏も壊れた。間もなく元号は慶長と改められた。
events.en: The Keichō Fushimi earthquake. A great quake struck Kyoto and the home provinces; the new keep of Fushimi castle fell and the great Buddha of Hōkōji was broken. Soon after, the era was renamed Keichō.

events.ja: 慶長の役。{r_oda}は再び朝鮮半島へ兵を送った。秀吉の死によって兵は引き揚げられた。
events.en: The Keichō campaign. {r_oda} sent troops to the peninsula again; they were withdrawn when Hideyoshi died.

events.ja: {n_utsunomiya}は秀吉に所領を取り上げられた。
events.en: {n_utsunomiya} lost its domain to Hideyoshi.

events.ja: {r_uesugi}は越後から会津百二十万石へ移された。
events.en: {r_uesugi} was moved from Echigo to Aizu, a domain of 1.2 million koku.

events.ja: 醍醐の花見。{r_oda}は醍醐寺に七百本の桜を植えさせ、秀頼・北政所・[[p:淀殿]]ら千三百人を招いて盛大な花見を催した。秀吉はこの年の秋に没する。
events.en: The cherry-blossom party at Daigo. {r_oda} had seven hundred cherry trees planted at Daigoji and held a great blossom-viewing for thirteen hundred guests, Hideyori, his wife and [[p:淀殿|Lady Yodo]] among them. He would die that autumn.

events.ja: 豊臣秀吉は伏見城で世を去った。「露と落ち露と消えにし我が身かな」。幼い秀頼の後見は[[p:徳川家康]]ら五大老と、[[p:石田三成]]ら五奉行に託された。
events.en: Toyotomi Hideyoshi died at Fushimi: "I came like dew, I vanish like dew." His small son Hideyori was left in the care of five elders, [[p:徳川家康|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] among them, and five commissioners led by [[p:石田三成|Ishida Mitsunari]].

events.ja: 大坂で[[p:前田利家]]が没した。その夜、[[p:加藤清正]]・[[p:福島正則]]ら七人の将が[[p:石田三成]]を討とうとした。三成は伏見に逃れ、家康の仲立ちで奉行を退いて近江の佐和山に引きこもった。
events.en: [[p:前田利家|Maeda Toshiie]] died at Osaka. That night seven captains, [[p:加藤清正|Katō Kiyomasa]] and [[p:福島正則|Fukushima Masanori]] among them, set out to kill [[p:石田三成|Ishida Mitsunari]]. He escaped to Fushimi and, through Ieyasu's mediation, gave up his office and withdrew to Sawayama in Ōmi.

events.ja: 小山評定。上杉を討つため下野の小山まで来た{r_tokugawa}のもとに、[[p:石田三成]]の挙兵の報せが届いた。従っていた大名たちは家康に付くことを決め、軍は西へ引き返した。
events.en: The council at Oyama. {r_tokugawa} had come as far as Oyama in Shimotsuke to strike the Uesugi when news came that [[p:石田三成|Ishida Mitsunari]] had raised an army. The lords with him resolved to stand by Ieyasu, and the army turned back west.

events.ja: 関ヶ原の戦い。[[p:徳川家康]]の東軍と[[p:石田三成]]の西軍が美濃の関ヶ原でぶつかった。昼過ぎ、[[p:小早川秀秋]]が東軍に寝返り、戦いは一日で決した。三成は捕らえられて斬られ、豊臣家は摂津・河内・和泉の一大名となった。
events.en: The battle of Sekigahara. [[p:徳川家康|Tokugawa Ieyasu]]'s eastern army met [[p:石田三成|Ishida Mitsunari]]'s western army at Sekigahara in Mino. Past noon [[p:小早川秀秋|Kobayakawa Hideaki]] went over to the east, and the day was decided. Mitsunari was caught and beheaded, and the Toyotomi were left a single domain of Settsu, Kawachi and Izumi.

events.ja: 長谷堂城の戦い。{r_uesugi}の[[p:直江兼続]]は二万余りで出羽に攻め入り、{r_mogami}の長谷堂城を囲んだ。城は半月持ちこたえ、関ヶ原で西軍が敗れたと知った兼続は兵を引いた。
events.en: The siege of Hasedō. [[p:直江兼続|Naoe Kanetsugu]] of {r_uesugi} invaded Dewa with over twenty thousand men and besieged Hasedō castle of {r_mogami}. It held for half a month; hearing that the west had lost at Sekigahara, Kanetsugu withdrew.

events.ja: 西軍の主力だった[[p:宇喜多秀家]]は所領を失い、のちに八丈島へ流された。
events.en: [[p:宇喜多秀家|Ukita Hideie]], a pillar of the western army, lost his domain and was later exiled to Hachijō island.

events.ja: 西軍の総大将に担がれた{r_mori}は、周防・長門の二国に減らされた。
events.en: {r_mori}, set up as commander of the western army, was cut down to Suō and Nagato.

events.ja: 西軍についた[[p:長宗我部盛親]]は土佐を取り上げられた。土佐は山内一豊に与えられた。
events.en: [[p:長宗我部盛親|Chōsokabe Morichika]], of the western army, lost Tosa; it was given to Yamauchi Kazutoyo.

events.ja: 西軍についた{n_onodera}は領地を失い、その地は最上家のものとなった。
events.en: {n_onodera}, which had sided with the west, lost its land to the Mogami.

events.ja: {r_date}は千代の地に城を築き、仙台と名を改めて移った。
events.en: {r_date} built a castle at Sendai — writing its name anew — and moved his seat there.

events.ja: 家康と争った{r_uesugi}は会津を取り上げられ、米沢三十万石に移された。
events.en: {r_uesugi}, who had defied Ieyasu, lost Aizu and was moved to Yonezawa with three hundred thousand koku.

events.ja: 関ヶ原で動かなかった{n_iwaki}は所領を取り上げられた。
events.en: {n_iwaki}, which had not moved at Sekigahara, lost its domain.

events.ja: 関ヶ原で去就のはっきりしなかった{r_satake}は、常陸五十四万石から出羽秋田二十万石に移された。秋田の{r_ando}は、入れ替わりに常陸宍戸に移された。
events.en: {r_satake}, who had not clearly taken a side at Sekigahara, was moved from 540,000 koku in Hitachi to 200,000 at Akita in Dewa; {r_ando} of Akita was moved to Shishido in Hitachi in exchange.

events.ja: 関ヶ原で敵中を突破して帰った島津家は、粘り強い交渉の末に本領を安堵された。
events.en: The Shimazu, who had cut their way out through the enemy at Sekigahara, kept their lands after long and stubborn talks.

events.ja: {r_tokugawa}は征夷大将軍に任じられ、江戸に幕府を開いた。
events.en: {r_tokugawa} was appointed shogun and opened his government in Edo.

events.ja: {r_tokugawa}は将軍の職を子の秀忠に譲った。将軍は徳川家が代々継ぐものと天下に示したのである。家康は大御所として、なお政を見た。
events.en: {r_tokugawa} handed the office of shogun to his son Hidetada, showing the realm that the Tokugawa would hold it from father to son. As retired shogun Ieyasu still ruled.

events.ja: 龍造寺家の実権は鍋島家に移り、佐賀は鍋島家の国となった。
events.en: Power in the Ryūzōji house passed to the Nabeshima, and Saga became the domain of the Nabeshima.

events.ja: {n_tsutsui}は家中の乱れを咎められて所領を失った。
events.en: {n_tsutsui} lost its domain for disorder in the house.

events.ja: {r_shimazu}は幕府の許しを得て三千の兵を琉球に送り、首里城を落として王を薩摩に連れ帰った。琉球はこののち、島津に従いながら明への朝貢も続けた。
events.en: With the shogunate's leave, {r_shimazu} sent three thousand men to Ryūkyū, took Shuri castle and brought the king back to Satsuma. From then on Ryūkyū served the Shimazu while still sending tribute to Ming.

events.ja: 二条城の会見。{r_tokugawa}は京の二条城で十九歳の{r_oda}と対面した。[[p:加藤清正]]らが秀頼に付き添った。立派に育った秀頼を見て家康は豊臣を除く心を固めた、と後の世には語られる。
events.en: The meeting at Nijō castle. {r_tokugawa} received the nineteen-year-old {r_oda} at Nijō castle in Kyoto, with [[p:加藤清正|Katō Kiyomasa]] and others in attendance. Later ages said that seeing how well Hideyori had grown, Ieyasu made up his mind to be rid of the Toyotomi.

events.ja: 慶長遣欧使節。{r_date}は家臣の[[p:支倉常長]]を、イスパニアとローマへの使いとして、領内で造った船で月ノ浦から送り出した。
events.en: The Keichō embassy. {r_date} sent his retainer [[p:支倉常長|Hasekura Tsunenaga]] as envoy to Spain and Rome, in a ship built in his own lands, from the harbour of Tsukinoura.

events.ja: 幕府は全国に[[a:kirisuto|キリスト教の禁教令]]を出した。宣教師や信徒の主だった者は国外へ追われた。
events.en: The shogunate [[a:kirisuto|banned Christianity]] throughout the land; the missionaries and leading believers were sent abroad.

events.ja: 方広寺鐘銘事件。{r_oda}が建て直した方広寺の大仏殿の鐘の銘「国家安康」「君臣豊楽」が、家康の名を断ち、豊臣を君とするものだと咎められた。弁明に赴いた片桐且元は大坂で疑われて城を去り、戦は避けられなくなった。
events.en: The affair of the Hōkōji bell. The inscription on the bell {r_oda} had cast for the rebuilt Hōkōji — "peace for the land, joy for lord and vassal" — was said to cut Ieyasu's name in two and hail the Toyotomi as lords. Katagiri Katsumoto, sent to explain, fell under suspicion at Osaka and left the castle; war could not now be avoided.

events.ja: {n_satomi}は幕府に領地を取り上げられ、伯耆へ移された。
events.en: The shogunate took the domain of {n_satomi} and sent its lord to Hōki.

events.ja: 大坂冬の陣。[[a:daibutsu|方広寺の鐘の銘]]を口実に、{r_tokugawa}は大坂城を囲んだ。[[p:真田信繁]]が城の南に築いた出丸 [[a:sanada_maru|(真田丸)]] は徳川の兵を寄せつけなかった。和が結ばれたが、大坂城の堀は埋められた。
events.en: The winter siege of Osaka. Taking offence at [[a:daibutsu|the inscription on a temple bell]], {r_tokugawa} besieged Osaka castle. [[a:sanada_maru|The outwork]] [[p:真田信繁|Sanada Nobushige]] built to the south held off every assault; a peace was made, but the castle's moats were filled in.

events.ja: 大坂夏の陣。堀を失った大坂城に籠もった豊臣方は城外に打って出た。[[p:真田信繁]]は家康の本陣に三度斬り込んだのち討たれ、城は燃え落ちた。[[p:豊臣秀頼]]と母の[[p:淀殿]]は自害し、豊臣家は滅んだ。
events.en: The summer siege of Osaka. With its moats gone, the Toyotomi side came out to fight in the open. [[p:真田信繁|Sanada Nobushige]] charged Ieyasu's headquarters three times before he was killed, and the castle burned. [[p:豊臣秀頼|Toyotomi Hideyori]] and his mother [[p:淀殿|Lady Yodo]] took their own lives, and the house of Toyotomi was no more.

events.ja: 元和偃武。大坂の陣ののち、幕府は[[a:buke_shohatto|一国一城令と武家諸法度]]を出した。応仁の乱から百五十年続いた戦乱の世は終わった。
events.en: The Genna peace. After Osaka the shogunate ordered [[a:buke_shohatto|one castle to a province]] and issued its laws for the warrior houses. The age of war that began with the Ōnin war a hundred and fifty years before was over.

deploy.ja: [[p:今川義元]]は二万五千と号する大軍で尾張へ入り、松平元康 (家康) らに大高城・鷲津・丸根の砦を攻めさせた。義元の本隊五千ほどは桶狭間の山あいで休息していた。[[p:織田信長]]は清洲から二千ほどで出た。
deploy.en: [[p:今川義元|Imagawa Yoshimoto]] entered Owari with a host said to number twenty-five thousand, and set [[p:まつ|Matsu]]daira Motoyasu (Ieyasu) and others against the Ōdaka castle and the forts of Washizu and Marune. Yoshimoto's own column, five thousand or so, rested in the hollows of Okehazama. [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]] rode out of Kiyosu with about two thousand.

plan.ja: 信長は夜明けに「敦盛」を舞って出陣し、熱田神宮で兵を集めた。砦が落ちたとの知らせを受けながら、善照寺砦から中島砦へ進み、昼過ぎの激しい雷雨の中を今川本隊に向かって突き進んだ。雨が上がった瞬間に襲いかかられた本隊は崩れ、義元は毛利新介に討たれた。
plan.en: Nobunaga danced "Atsumori" at dawn and rode out, gathering his men at the Atsuta shrine. Hearing the forts had fallen, he pushed on from Zenshōji to Nakajima and, in a violent thunderstorm after noon, drove straight at the Imagawa column. It broke the moment the rain stopped and he fell on it; Yoshimoto was cut down by Mōri Shinsuke.

tales.ja: 「人間五十年、下天のうちをくらぶれば、夢幻のごとくなり」。出陣の朝、信長は幸若舞「敦盛」のこの一節を舞い、湯漬けをかき込んで、わずかな供と城を飛び出したという。
tales.en: "Fifty years of a man's life, beside the realm below heaven, are a dream, an illusion." On the morning he rode out Nobunaga danced these lines from the ballad Atsumori, gulped a bowl of rice in hot water and dashed from the castle with a handful of men.

tales.ja: 義元を討った毛利新介は、首を取るとき義元に指を食いちぎられたと伝わる。
tales.en: Mōri Shinsuke, who killed Yoshimoto, is said to have lost a finger, bitten off by Yoshimoto as he took his head.

after.ja: 今川家は大きく揺らぎ、松平元康は岡崎で自立した。信長の名は一夜で天下に知られた。
after.en: The Imagawa house was shaken to its roots and [[p:まつ|Matsu]]daira Motoyasu made himself independent at Okazaki. Overnight Nobunaga's name was known throughout the land.

deploy.ja: [[p:上杉謙信]]は妻女山に陣取り、[[p:武田信玄]]は海津城に入った。武田は兵を二つに分け、[[p:高坂昌信]]・[[p:馬場信春]]らの別働隊一万二千が妻女山を背後から突き、信玄の本隊八千が八幡原で待ち受けることにした。
deploy.en: [[p:上杉謙信|Uesugi Kenshin]] camped on Mount Saijo; [[p:武田信玄|Takeda Shingen]] entered Kaizu castle. Takeda split his army: a detachment of twelve thousand under [[p:高坂昌信|Kōsaka Masanobu]] and [[p:馬場信春|Baba Nobuharu]] would strike the mountain from behind, while Shingen's main body of eight thousand waited on the plain of Hachimanbara.

plan.ja: [[p:山本勘助]]の「啄木鳥の戦法」(木をつついて飛び出した虫を食う) であったが、謙信は海津城から上がる炊煙の多さで動きを見抜き、夜のうちに山を下りて霧の八幡原に陣を敷いた。霧が晴れると、目の前に上杉の全軍がいた。上杉は「車懸り」で次々と新手を繰り出し、武田の本隊は崩れかけたが、別働隊が駆けつけて上杉を挟んだ。
plan.en: It was [[p:山本勘助|Yamamoto Kansuke]]'s "woodpecker" plan — peck at the tree and catch the insects that fly out. But Kenshin read it from the many cooking fires smoking over Kaizu, came down the mountain by night and drew up in the fog on Hachimanbara. When the fog lifted, Shingen found the whole Uesugi army before him. The Uesugi sent in fresh troops wave on wave; the Takeda main body was close to breaking when the detachment arrived and caught the Uesugi between them.

tales.ja: 白い頭巾の騎馬武者がただ一騎、信玄の本陣に斬り込み、床几に座る信玄に三太刀を浴びせた。信玄は軍配で受け止めたと伝わる (一騎討ちは後の軍記の語るところ)。
tales.en: A horseman in a white hood rode alone into Shingen's camp and slashed three times at Shingen on his stool, who caught the blows on his war fan — so the later war tales tell.

tales.ja: 信玄の弟[[p:武田信繁]]と軍師[[p:山本勘助]]は、この戦いで討死した。信繁の家訓は、のちの武士の手本とされた。
tales.en: Shingen's brother [[p:武田信繁|Takeda Nobushige]] and his strategist [[p:山本勘助|Yamamoto Kansuke]] were killed in the battle; Nobushige's house rules were later held up as a model for warriors.

after.ja: 両軍とも多くを失い、勝敗ははっきりしなかった。北信濃は武田のものとして残った。
after.en: Both sides lost heavily and neither clearly won; northern Shinano stayed Takeda land.

name.en: the battle of the Ane river

deploy.ja: 織田・徳川の連合軍は姉川の南に陣し、北岸に浅井・朝倉の連合軍が並んだ。徳川は朝倉、織田は浅井と向き合った。
deploy.en: Oda and Tokugawa drew up south of the Ane; Azai and Asakura faced them on the north bank. Tokugawa took on Asakura, Oda the Azai.

plan.ja: 浅井の磯野員昌は織田の陣を十三段のうち十一段まで突き崩したと伝わる。だが徳川勢が朝倉を押し返し、[[p:榊原康政]]が横から朝倉を突いて崩すと、浅井も支えきれずに退いた。
plan.en: Isono Kazumasa of the Azai is said to have broken eleven of the thirteen lines of the Oda array. But the Tokugawa pushed the Asakura back, [[p:榊原康政|Sakakibara Yasumasa]] took them in the flank, and when the Asakura broke the Azai could not hold either.

tales.ja: 姉川の水は血で赤く染まり、のちに「血原」「血川」と呼ばれる地名が残ったという。
tales.en: The waters of the Ane ran red, and places there were called "the Field of Blood" and "the River of Blood" ever after, they say.

after.ja: 浅井・朝倉は敗れたものの滅びず、本願寺や武田と結んで信長を包囲していく。
after.en: Azai and Asakura were beaten but not destroyed; with the Ishiyama believers and the Takeda they went on to encircle Nobunaga.

deploy.ja: 西へ進む[[p:武田信玄]]の大軍は、浜松城を素通りして三方ヶ原の台地へ上がった。家康は織田の援軍を合わせ一万一千で城を出て、背後を襲おうとした。
deploy.en: Shingen's great army marched west past Hamamatsu castle and climbed onto the Mikatagahara plateau. Ieyasu came out with eleven thousand, Oda reinforcements included, to fall on its rear.

plan.ja: 武田は台地の上で振り返り、「魚鱗」の陣で待ち受けていた。家康は横に広い「鶴翼」で挑んだが、夕暮れから二時間ほどで崩れ、浜松城へ逃げ戻った。
plan.en: On the plateau the Takeda turned and waited in a "fish scale" wedge. Ieyasu came on in a wide "crane's wing" and in two hours of dusk was broken and fled back to Hamamatsu.

tales.ja: 城に戻った家康は、門を開けたままかがり火を焚かせた (空城の計)。追ってきた[[p:山県昌景]]は罠を疑って引き返したという。
tales.en: Back in the castle Ieyasu had the gates left open and bonfires lit; pursuing, [[p:山県昌景|Yamagata Masakage]] suspected a trap and turned back, it is said.

tales.ja: 家康はこの敗戦の苦い顔を絵師に描かせ、慢心の戒めとしたと伝わる (いわゆる「しかみ像」。この由来は後世の言い伝えともいう)。
tales.en: Ieyasu is said to have had a painter draw his face twisted with the bitterness of this defeat, as a warning against pride — though the story behind the portrait may be a later tradition.

after.ja: 信玄はそのまま西へ進んだが、翌年の春に病に倒れ、甲斐へ帰る途中で世を去った。
after.en: Shingen marched on west, but fell ill the next spring and died on the way home to Kai.

deploy.ja: [[p:武田勝頼]]は長篠城を囲んだ。救援に来た織田・徳川は設楽原の連吾川沿いに陣を敷き、川の手前に二重三重の馬防柵を築いた。
deploy.en: [[p:武田勝頼|Takeda Katsuyori]] besieged Nagashino castle. The Oda and Tokugawa came to relieve it and drew up along the Rengo stream at Shitaragahara, building double and triple palisades against horse in front of it.

plan.ja: 織田の[[p:酒井忠次]]の別働隊が夜のうちに鳶ノ巣山砦を奪い、武田は背後を断たれた。勝頼は決戦を選び、[[p:山県昌景]]らの軍勢が柵に向かって次々と攻めかかったが、柵の内から撃ちかけられる多数の鉄砲と弓に阻まれた。昼過ぎまでに武田の名将の多くが討たれた。
plan.en: A detachment under [[p:酒井忠次|Sakai Tadatsugu]] took the Tobinosuyama fort by night, cutting the Takeda off behind. Katsuyori chose battle; [[p:山県昌景|Yamagata Masakage]] and the rest charged the palisades wave after wave, and were stopped by the guns and bows firing from behind them. By early afternoon most of Takeda's great captains were dead.

tales.ja: 「鉄砲三千挺の三段撃ち」は後世の軍記が広めた話で、実際の数や撃ち方ははっきりしない。それでも多くの鉄砲を柵とともに使ったことは確かとされる。
tales.en: "Three thousand guns firing in three ranks" is a tale spread by later war chronicles; the true numbers and drill are uncertain. That many guns were used together with the palisades is beyond doubt.

tales.ja: 長篠城では、援軍を求めて城を抜け出した鳥居強右衛門が武田に捕らえられ、「援軍は来ない」と城に叫ぶよう命じられた。彼は「援軍はすぐ来る」と叫び、磔にされた。
tales.en: At Nagashino castle, Torii Suneemon slipped out to fetch help, was caught by the Takeda and ordered to shout to the castle that no help was coming. He shouted that help was near, and was crucified.

after.ja: 武田は山県・馬場・内藤らを失い、急速に力を落とした。七年後、武田家は滅ぶ。
after.en: Takeda lost Yamagata, Baba, Naitō and many more, and its strength drained away; seven years later the house was gone.

name.en: the battle of the Mimi river

deploy.ja: [[p:大友宗麟]]は日向に大軍を送り、島津方の高城を囲ませた。[[p:島津義久]]は救援に向かい、高城川 (小丸川) を挟んで大友軍と対した。
deploy.en: [[p:大友宗麟|Ōtomo Sōrin]] sent a great army into Hyūga to besiege the Shimazu castle of Taka; [[p:島津義久|Shimazu Yoshihisa]] came to its aid and faced the Ōtomo across the Takajō river.

plan.ja: 功を焦る[[p:田北鎮周]]が川を渡って攻めかかると、島津は少数の囮を退かせ、伏せていた左右の兵で包み込んだ (釣り野伏せ)。崩れた大友軍は耳川まで追われ、増水した川で多くが溺れた。
plan.en: The impatient [[p:田北鎮周|Tagita Shigekane]] crossed and attacked; the Shimazu let a small decoy fall back and closed on the pursuers with men hidden on both sides — the "fishing ambush". The broken Ōtomo army was chased to the Mimi river, where many drowned in the flood.

tales.ja: 大友軍の将たちは仲が悪く、総大将の[[p:田原紹忍]]は戦いの最中も采配が定まらなかったという。
tales.en: The Ōtomo generals were at odds, and their commander [[p:田原紹忍|Tawara Jōnin]] could not settle on orders even as the battle went on.

after.ja: 大友は多くの重臣を失い、島津は九州の覇権を目指して北上する。
after.en: Ōtomo lost many of its leading men; the Shimazu turned north, aiming for mastery of Kyūshū.

deploy.ja: [[p:龍造寺隆信]]は[[p:有馬晴信]]を攻めた。[[p:島津家久]]はわずかな兵で有馬を助け、湿地の中を細い畷 (あぜ道) が通る沖田に陣を敷いた。
deploy.en: [[p:龍造寺隆信|Ryūzōji Takanobu]] marched on [[p:有馬晴信|Arima Harunobu]]. [[p:島津家久|Shimazu Iehisa]] came to Arima's aid with a small force and took his stand at Okita, where narrow causeways ran through the marsh.

plan.ja: 大軍の龍造寺勢は細い道に縦長に伸び、湿地に足を取られた。島津は囮で誘い込み、左右の茂みから鉄砲と弓で撃ちかけて斬り込んだ。乱戦の中で隆信は討たれた。
plan.en: The great Ryūzōji army stretched thin along the narrow paths and bogged down in the marsh. The Shimazu drew it in with a decoy and struck from the thickets on both sides with guns and bows, then swords. In the melee Takanobu was killed.

tales.ja: 肥満で馬に乗れなかった隆信は、六人担ぎの輿に乗って戦場に出ていたと伝わる。
tales.en: Takanobu, too stout to ride, is said to have gone into battle in a palanquin carried by six men.

after.ja: 龍造寺は島津に従い、九州は島津・大友の争いとなった。
after.en: Ryūzōji bowed to the Shimazu, and Kyūshū was left to Shimazu and Ōtomo.

deploy.ja: 織田信雄と結んだ家康は小牧山に陣を構え、秀吉は大軍で対した。両軍とも砦を築いて睨み合った。
deploy.en: Allied with Oda Nobukatsu, Ieyasu fortified Mount Komaki; Hideyoshi faced him with a far larger army, and both sides dug in behind their forts.

plan.ja: [[p:池田恒興]]らは手薄な家康の本国三河を突く「中入り」を進言し、二万の別働隊が動いた。家康はこれを察してひそかに追い、長久手で別働隊を破って池田恒興と森長可を討ち取った。
plan.en: [[p:池田恒興|Ikeda Tsuneoki]] proposed a raid deep into Ieyasu's home province of Mikawa, and a detachment of twenty thousand set out. Ieyasu saw it, followed in secret, and destroyed it at Nagakute, killing Ikeda Tsuneoki and Mori Nagayoshi.

tales.ja: [[p:井伊直政]]の部隊は甲冑を赤一色に揃えた「赤備え」で、敵に恐れられたという。
tales.en: [[p:井伊直政|Ii Naomasa]]'s men wore armour all in red — the "red guard" — and their enemies dreaded them.

after.ja: 秀吉は戦いでは勝てなかったが、信雄と単独で和を結んで家康の大義名分を奪った。家康はのちに秀吉に臣従する。
after.en: Hideyoshi could not win in the field, but made a separate peace with Nobukatsu and took away Ieyasu's cause; Ieyasu later bowed to him.

plan.ja: [[p:伊達政宗]]は磐梯山の麓、摺上原で[[p:蘆名義広]]と戦った。初めは向かい風に砂塵を浴びて苦しんだが、風向きが変わると攻勢に転じ、蘆名勢を日橋川へ追い落とした。
plan.en: [[p:伊達政宗|Date Masamune]] met [[p:蘆名義広|Ashina Yoshihiro]] at Suriagehara under Mount Bandai. At first the wind drove dust into his men's faces; when it turned, he went over to the attack and drove the Ashina into the Nippashi river.

tales.ja: 蘆名家中には政宗に内通した者が多く、戦いの最中に兵を動かさない家臣もいたという。
tales.en: Many in the Ashina house were secretly in touch with Masamune, and some of its men never moved during the battle.

after.ja: 政宗は会津を得て南奥州の大半を手にしたが、翌年の小田原征伐に遅参し、秀吉に会津を取り上げられる。
after.en: Masamune won Aizu and most of southern Ōu — and the next year, late to the siege of Odawara, lost Aizu to Hideyoshi.

deploy.ja: 西軍は[[p:石田三成]]・[[p:宇喜多秀家]]・[[p:小西行長]]・[[p:大谷吉継]]らが関ヶ原の西に陣を敷き、南の松尾山に[[p:小早川秀秋]]、東の南宮山に毛利秀元・吉川広家らが陣取って、東軍を包み込む形をとった。東軍は[[p:福島正則]]を先鋒に、家康は桃配山に本陣を置いた。
deploy.en: The western army — [[p:石田三成|Ishida Mitsunari]], [[p:宇喜多秀家|Ukita Hideie]], [[p:小西行長|Konishi Yukinaga]], [[p:大谷吉継|Ōtani Yoshitsugu]] and others — drew up on the west side of Sekigahara, with [[p:小早川秀秋|Kobayakawa Hideaki]] on Mount [[p:まつ|Matsu]]o to the south and Mōri Hidemoto and Kikkawa Hiroie on Mount Nangū to the east, as if to enfold the eastern army. The east sent [[p:福島正則|Fukushima Masanori]] forward; Ieyasu set his headquarters on Mount Momokubari.

plan.ja: 朝の霧の中、[[p:井伊直政]]の抜け駆けで戦いが始まった。西軍は善戦し、昼まで一進一退が続いた。毛利勢は吉川広家が東軍と通じていて動かず、松尾山の[[p:小早川秀秋]]も動かなかった。昼過ぎ、家康が松尾山に鉄砲を撃ちかけると (問鉄砲。後世の話ともいう)、秀秋は東軍に寝返って[[p:大谷吉継]]の陣に攻め下った。脇坂ら四将も寝返り、西軍は総崩れとなった。
plan.en: In the morning fog [[p:井伊直政|Ii Naomasa]] jumped the start and the battle began. The west fought well, and until noon neither side gave way. The Mōri did not move — Kikkawa Hiroie had a secret understanding with the east — and neither did Kobayakawa on Mount [[p:まつ|Matsu]]o. After noon Ieyasu had guns fired at the mountain (a later story, some say); Hideaki went over to the east and charged down on [[p:大谷吉継|Ōtani Yoshitsugu]]. Four more commanders turned, and the western army collapsed.

tales.ja: 病で目が見えなくなっていた[[p:大谷吉継]]は、寝返りを予期して備えていたが支えきれず自害した。親友の[[p:石田三成]]の頼みで、負けを承知で西軍に加わっていたという。
tales.en: [[p:大谷吉継|Ōtani Yoshitsugu]], half blind with illness, had foreseen the betrayal and prepared for it, but could not hold, and took his own life. He had joined the west knowing it would lose, they say, because his friend [[p:石田三成|Ishida Mitsunari]] asked him.

tales.ja: [[p:島津義弘]]は敵中を正面突破して退却した (島津の退き口)。甥の豊久らが次々と殿に残って討たれ、千五百の兵のうち薩摩に帰り着いたのは数十人であったという。
tales.en: [[p:島津義弘|Shimazu Yoshihiro]] retreated by cutting straight through the enemy — "the Shimazu withdrawal". His nephew Toyohisa and others stayed behind one after another to hold the pursuers and died; of fifteen hundred men only a few dozen reached Satsuma.

tales.ja: 捕らえられた三成は、処刑の前に喉が渇いて湯を求め、代わりに干し柿を勧められると「痰の毒だ」と断った。「大志を抱く者は最期まで命を惜しむ」と言ったという。
tales.en: Captured, Mitsunari asked for hot water before his execution; offered a dried persimmon instead, he refused it as bad for the phlegm. "A man with great aims guards his life to the end," he said.

after.ja: 戦いは一日で終わり、家康は西軍の大名の領地を取り上げて味方に分け与えた。三年後、家康は征夷大将軍となる。
after.en: The battle was over in a day. Ieyasu stripped the western daimyo of their lands and handed them to his own side; three years later he was shogun.

deploy.ja: 冬の陣の和議で堀を埋められた大坂城は守れず、豊臣方は城を出て天王寺・岡山口に陣を敷いた。家康は天王寺口、秀忠は岡山口から攻めた。
deploy.en: With its moats filled in after the winter peace, Osaka castle could not be held; the Toyotomi side came out and drew up at Tennōji and Okayama. Ieyasu attacked at Tennōji, Hidetada at Okayama.

plan.ja: [[p:真田信繁]]は天王寺口から家康の本陣めがけて突撃し、三度にわたって斬り込んで本陣の旗を倒した。家康は一時、自害を覚悟したとも伝わる。だが数に勝る徳川勢が押し返し、信繁は安居神社で討たれた。城には火が放たれた。
plan.en: [[p:真田信繁|Sanada Nobushige]] charged from Tennōji straight at Ieyasu's headquarters, broke in three times and brought down its standard; Ieyasu, some say, was ready to kill himself. But the larger Tokugawa army pushed back, and Nobushige was killed at the Yasui shrine. The castle was set on fire.

tales.ja: [[p:真田信繁]]を敵方の島津家の記録は「日本一の兵」と讃えた。
tales.en: The records of the Shimazu, on the other side, called [[p:真田信繁|Sanada Nobushige]] "the finest soldier in Japan".

tales.ja: 秀頼と[[p:淀殿]]は山里曲輪の蔵に籠もり、助命の願いが聞き入れられないと知って自害した。
tales.en: Hideyori and [[p:淀殿|Lady Yodo]] shut themselves in a storehouse in the inner citadel, and when they learned no mercy would be given, took their own lives.

after.ja: 豊臣家は滅び、元号は元和と改められた。応仁の乱から続いた戦乱の世は終わった。
after.en: The house of Toyotomi was gone and the era was renamed Genna. The age of war that had begun with the Ōnin war was over.

deploy.ja: 小田原城を四日囲んで引き揚げた武田軍が相模の三増峠を越えようとすると、[[p:北条綱成]]・氏照・氏邦らが先回りして峠の下に陣を敷いた。小田原からも氏政の本隊が追ってきていた。
deploy.en: The Takeda, withdrawing after four days before Odawara, made for Mimase pass in Sagami; [[p:北条綱成|Hōjō Tsunashige]], Ujiteru and Ujikuni got there first and drew up below the pass, and Ujimasa's main army was following from Odawara.

plan.ja: 信玄は荷駄を守りつつ峠に陣を取り、[[p:山県昌景]]の別働隊を山伝いに北条勢の横へ回り込ませた。正面で押し合ううちに別働隊が山の上から攻め下り、北条勢は崩れた。氏政の本隊は間に合わなかった。
plan.en: Shingen held the pass while guarding his baggage and sent [[p:山県昌景|Yamagata Masakage]]'s detachment along the ridges onto the Hōjō flank. While the fronts pushed against each other, the detachment came down from the heights and the Hōjō broke; Ujimasa's army arrived too late.

after.ja: 武田軍は甲斐へ帰り着き、駿河をめぐる武田と北条の争いは続いた。武田方でも浅利信種が討たれた。
after.en: The Takeda reached Kai, and the struggle for Suruga went on. On the Takeda side Asari Nobutane had fallen.

name.ja: 第一次木津川口の戦い
name.en: the first battle of the Kizu river mouth

deploy.ja: 織田に囲まれた石山本願寺へ兵糧を運ぶため、毛利と村上の水軍がおよそ八百艘で大坂湾に現れた。織田方の水軍三百艘余りが木津川の河口で待ち受けた。
deploy.en: To carry rice into the besieged Ishiyama Honganji, the Mōri and Murakami navies — some eight hundred boats — appeared in Osaka Bay. Over three hundred Oda boats waited at the mouth of the Kizu river.

plan.ja: 毛利の水軍は焙烙火矢 (火薬を詰めた焼き玉) を次々と投げ込み、織田の船を焼き払った。織田方の将の多くが討たれ、兵糧は無事に石山へ運び込まれた。
plan.en: The Mōri crews threw fire-pots — clay balls packed with powder — one after another and burned the Oda fleet. Many Oda captains died, and the rice went safely into Ishiyama.

after.ja: 石山の籠城は続いた。信長は焼けない船を造るよう[[p:九鬼嘉隆]]に命じた。
after.en: The siege of Ishiyama dragged on. Nobunaga ordered [[p:九鬼嘉隆|Kuki Yoshitaka]] to build ships that would not burn.

name.en: the battle of the Tedori river

deploy.ja: 七尾城を救うため、[[p:柴田勝家]]の率いる織田の大軍が加賀の手取川を越えて進んだ。[[p:羽柴秀吉]]は勝家と争って陣を離れていた。軍が川を越えたのち、七尾城はすでに落ちていたと知らされた。
deploy.en: [[p:柴田勝家|Shibata Katsuie]] led the great Oda army across the Tedori river in Kaga to relieve Nanao — [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hashiba Hideyoshi]] had quarrelled with him and left. Across the river they learned that Nanao had already fallen.

plan.ja: 勝家は兵を引こうとしたが、謙信はすばやく南へ下って退く織田軍に夜襲をかけた。雨で水かさの増した手取川を背にした織田軍は、多くが川に追い落とされて溺れた。
plan.en: Katsuie turned back, but Kenshin came south fast and struck the retreating army by night. With the rain-swollen Tedori at its back, many of the Oda men were driven into the river and drowned.

tales.ja: 謙信は「信長は聞いていたほど強くない。これなら天下へ攻め上るのもたやすい」と書き送ったと伝わる。のちに「聞くと見るとは大違い、案外弱い信長」と戯れ歌にもなった。
tales.en: Kenshin wrote, it is said, that Nobunaga was not as strong as he had heard, and the march on the capital would be easy; it later became a mocking ditty.

after.ja: 能登と加賀の北半分は上杉のものとなった。だが謙信は翌年の春、次の出陣を前に急に倒れて没した。
after.en: Noto and northern Kaga became Uesugi land. But the next spring, on the eve of another campaign, Kenshin suddenly collapsed and died.

name.ja: 第二次木津川口の戦い
name.en: the second battle of the Kizu river mouth

deploy.ja: [[p:九鬼嘉隆]]は伊勢で造った六艘の大船を大坂湾に回した。船体を鉄の板で覆い、大筒を積んでいたと伝わる。そこへ石山へ兵糧を運ぶ毛利の水軍六百艘が攻め寄せた。
deploy.en: [[p:九鬼嘉隆|Kuki Yoshitaka]] brought six great ships built in Ise round to Osaka Bay — clad in iron plates, it is said, and carrying cannon. Six hundred Mōri boats came on, bringing rice to Ishiyama.

plan.ja: 毛利の船は前と同じく焙烙火矢を投げたが、大船は燃えなかった。九鬼の大船は敵の大将の船を引き寄せて大筒で撃ち砕き、毛利の水軍は退いた。
plan.en: The Mōri threw their fire-pots as before, but the great ships would not burn. Kuki let the enemy flagships draw close and shattered them with his cannon, and the Mōri navy fell back.

after.ja: 大坂湾の海路は断たれ、石山本願寺は兵糧に窮していった。一年余りのちに和が結ばれる。
after.en: The sea road into Osaka Bay was cut and Ishiyama Honganji began to starve; peace came a year and more later.

deploy.ja: 浅井を救いに近江へ出た[[p:朝倉義景]]は、嵐の夜に織田に砦を落とされて越前へ退き始めた。信長は「朝倉は必ず退く」と家臣に命じ、自ら先頭に立って追った。
deploy.en: [[p:朝倉義景|Asakura Yoshikage]], who had come into Ōmi to save the Azai, began to fall back to Echizen after the Oda took his forts on a stormy night. Nobunaga, having told his captains that the Asakura were sure to withdraw, led the pursuit himself.

plan.ja: 織田軍は越前へ通じる刀根坂で朝倉軍に追いつき、退く兵をつぎつぎに討った。朝倉方の名だたる将の多くがここで討死した。
plan.en: The Oda caught the Asakura on the Tonezaka road into Echizen and cut down the retreating men by the hundred; many of the best-known Asakura captains died there.

after.ja: 織田軍はそのまま越前に攻め入り、一乗谷を焼いた。義景は一族の景鏡に背かれて自害した。
after.en: The Oda went straight on into Echizen and burned Ichijōdani; betrayed by his kinsman Kageakira, Yoshikage took his life.

deploy.ja: 二本松の畠山義継に父輝宗を連れ去られて失った政宗は、弔い合戦として二本松城を囲んだ。畠山を救うため、[[p:佐竹義重]]と蘆名・岩城・石川・白河らの連合軍およそ三万が南から攻め上った。
deploy.en: Masamune had lost his father Terumune, carried off by Hatakeyama Yoshitsugu of Nihonmatsu, and laid siege to Nihonmatsu in revenge. To save it, [[p:佐竹義重|Satake Yoshishige]] came north with the Ashina, Iwaki, Ishikawa and Shirakawa — some thirty thousand men.

plan.ja: 伊達勢は観音堂山に本陣を置き、瀬戸川に架かる人取橋のあたりで迎え撃った。数に勝る連合軍に押され、政宗の本陣にまで敵が迫った。老臣の鬼庭左月は殿 (しんがり) を務めて討死し、[[p:伊達成実]]の奮戦でようやく持ちこたえた。
plan.en: The Date set their headquarters on Kannondō hill and met the enemy around the Hitotori bridge over the Seto river. The allies, far more numerous, pressed all the way to Masamune's own lines; the old retainer Oniwa Sagetsu died holding the rear, and [[p:伊達成実|Date Shigezane]]'s stand barely held the field.

after.ja: その夜、佐竹の本国が背後を脅かされたとの報せが届き、連合軍は兵を引いた。政宗は危ういところで救われ、翌年二本松を手に入れた。
after.en: That night word came that the Satake homeland was threatened from behind, and the allies withdrew. Masamune was saved by a hair, and took Nihonmatsu the next year.

name.en: the battle of the Hetsugi river

deploy.ja: 島津に攻められた大友を救うため、秀吉は四国の[[p:長宗我部元親]]・信親、十河存保らを先に豊後へ送り、仙石秀久を軍監とした。[[p:島津家久]]は鶴賀城を囲み、戸次川の向こうに陣を敷いた。
deploy.en: To save the Ōtomo from the Shimazu, Hideyoshi sent the Shikoku lords ahead into Bungo — [[p:長宗我部元親|Chōsokabe Motochika]] and Nobuchika, Sogō Masayasu and others — with Sengoku Hidehisa as overseer. [[p:島津家久|Shimazu Iehisa]] was besieging Tsurugajō, camped across the Hetsugi river.

plan.ja: 元親は援軍を待つべきだと説いたが、仙石は川を渡って攻めることを押し通した。島津は得意の「釣り野伏せ」で、退くと見せて敵を引き込み、伏せた兵で三方から包んだ。
plan.en: Motochika urged waiting for the main army, but Sengoku insisted on crossing the river to attack. The Shimazu used their favourite trick — feign a retreat, draw the enemy in, and close on them from three sides with hidden troops.

after.ja: 信親と十河存保は討死し、仙石は真っ先に逃げ帰って領地を取り上げられた。元親は最愛の嫡男を失い、人が変わったようになったという。島津は府内を落とした。
after.en: Nobuchika and Sogō Masayasu fell; Sengoku fled first of all and was stripped of his lands. Motochika, having lost his beloved heir, seemed a changed man. The Shimazu took Funai.

deploy.ja: 家康が西へ引き返すと、上杉の[[p:直江兼続]]は二万余りを率いて出羽に攻め入り、最上の城を次々と落として、山形城の手前の長谷堂城を囲んだ。城には志村光安ら千ほどが籠もった。
deploy.en: When Ieyasu turned back west, [[p:直江兼続|Naoe Kanetsugu]] of the Uesugi invaded Dewa with over twenty thousand men, took Mogami castle after castle and besieged Hasedō, the last before Yamagata. Some thousand men under Shimura Akiyasu held it.

plan.ja: 城の周りの深田に阻まれて上杉の兵は攻めあぐね、城兵の夜襲も受けた。[[p:最上義光]]は伊達の援軍とともに城の後ろに陣を張り、半月の間、城は落ちなかった。
plan.en: The deep paddy fields round the castle bogged the Uesugi down, and the garrison raided them by night. [[p:最上義光|Mogami Yoshiaki]] camped behind the castle with Date reinforcements, and for half a month it did not fall.

after.ja: 関ヶ原で西軍が一日で敗れたとの報せが届き、兼続は兵を引いた。最上勢の激しい追撃を、兼続は自ら殿に立って防ぎ、米沢へ帰り着いた。
after.en: News came that the west had lost at Sekigahara in a single day, and Kanetsugu withdrew; he held the rear himself against the fierce Mogami pursuit and got home to Yonezawa.

deploy.ja: 大坂城は三方を川と海に守られ、南だけが平地に開けていた。[[p:真田信繁]]はその南の外に出丸を築き、五千ほどで籠もった。徳川方は前田・井伊・松平らの軍を南に並べた。
deploy.en: Osaka castle was guarded by rivers and the sea on three sides, open only to the south. [[p:真田信繁|Sanada Nobushige]] built an outwork beyond its southern wall and held it with some five thousand men; the Tokugawa set the Maeda, Ii and [[p:まつ|Matsu]]daira armies along the south.

plan.ja: 真田勢は前の篠山から鉄砲を撃ちかけて挑み、怒って空堀に押し寄せた徳川方の兵を、出丸の上から鉄砲でさんざんに撃った。城内で火薬の事故が起きたのを内通の合図と取り違えた兵がさらに押し寄せ、損害はますます大きくなった。
plan.en: The Sanada provoked them with fire from Sasayama in front; the angered Tokugawa men poured into the dry moat and were shot down from the outwork. A powder accident inside the castle was mistaken for a traitor's signal, more men pressed in, and the losses mounted.

after.ja: 家康は力攻めをやめて大筒で城を撃たせ、和を結んだ。和の条件として大坂城の堀は埋められ、真田丸も壊された。
after.en: Ieyasu gave up storming the castle, bombarded it with cannon and made peace. Under its terms the moats of Osaka were filled in and the Sanada-maru pulled down.

terms.ja: 今川軍は駿河へ引き揚げ、尾張の今川方の城も次々と織田に下った。
terms.en: The Imagawa army went home to Suruga, and the Imagawa castles in Owari went over to Oda one by one.

terms.ja: 両軍とも兵を引いた。上杉・武田の対陣はこの後も続くが、北信濃は武田のものとして落ち着いた。
terms.en: Both armies drew off. Uesugi and Takeda would face each other again, but northern Shinano settled as Takeda land.

name.ja: 駿河をめぐる武田・北条の戦い

terms.ja: [[p:北条氏康]]は死に臨んで武田と和するよう言い残し、氏政は再び武田と同盟を結んだ。駿河は武田のものと決まった。
terms.en: [[p:北条氏康|Hōjō Ujiyasu]], dying, told his son to make peace with the Takeda; Ujimasa renewed the alliance, and Suruga was left to the Takeda.

terms.ja: 信玄は三河の野田城を落とした後に病が重くなり、甲斐へ帰る途中、信濃の駒場で没した。死は三年秘すよう遺言された。
terms.en: After taking Noda castle in Mikawa Shingen fell gravely ill and died at Komaba in Shinano on the way home; he left word that his death be kept secret three years.

terms.ja: 刀根坂で敗れた[[p:朝倉義景]]は一乗谷を焼かれ、一族の景鏡に背かれて自害した。朝倉家は滅んだ。
terms.en: Beaten at Tonezaka, [[p:朝倉義景|Asakura Yoshikage]] saw Ichijōdani burned, was betrayed by his kinsman Kageakira and killed himself. The Asakura house was gone.

terms.ja: 小谷城は落ち、[[p:浅井長政]]は自害した。妻の[[p:お市]]と三人の娘は織田の陣へ送り届けられた。
terms.en: Odani castle fell and [[p:浅井長政|Azai Nagamasa]] took his life; his wife [[p:お市|Oichi]] and their three daughters were sent safely to the Oda camp.

terms.ja: 長島の砦は兵糧攻めで次々と落ち、降伏を申し出た門徒も許されなかった。
terms.en: The Nagashima forts fell one by one to starvation, and even the believers who offered to surrender were not spared.

terms.ja: 武田軍は甲斐へ退いた。徳川は奥三河と遠江の城を次々に取り返していく。
terms.en: The Takeda army went back to Kai, and Tokugawa won back the castles of Okumikawa and Tōtōmi one after another.

name.ja: 大友・島津の日向の戦い
name.en: the Hyūga war of Ōtomo and Shimazu

terms.ja: 大友軍は豊後へ逃げ帰り、日向は島津のものとなった。
terms.en: The Ōtomo army fled back to Bungo and Hyūga became Shimazu land.

terms.ja: 天皇の仲立ちで和が結ばれ、[[p:顕如]]は石山を出て紀伊の鷺森へ移った。石山はやがて炎上した。
terms.en: Peace was made through the emperor's good offices; [[p:顕如|Kennyo]] left Ishiyama for Saginomori in Kii, and Ishiyama later went up in flames.

terms.ja: 備中高松城を水攻めにしていた[[p:羽柴秀吉]]は本能寺の変を知ると、城主清水宗治の切腹を条件に毛利と急ぎ和を結び、京へ引き返した。
terms.en: [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hashiba Hideyoshi]], flooding Takamatsu castle in Bitchū, heard of Honnōji and hurried into peace with the Mōri — the castle lord Shimizu Muneharu to take his own life — then turned back for Kyoto.

terms.ja: 越中の魚津城は織田の大軍の前に落ちたが、本能寺の変の報せに[[p:柴田勝家]]らの北陸勢は兵を引き、上杉は滅亡を免れた。
terms.en: Uozu castle in Etchū fell to the great Oda army, but at the news of Honnōji [[p:柴田勝家|Shibata Katsuie]] and the northern army withdrew, and the Uesugi were spared.

name.ja: 島原の戦い (島津・龍造寺)

terms.ja: 当主を失った龍造寺家は島津に従い、[[p:鍋島直茂]]が家を支えた。
terms.en: Its lord dead, the Ryūzōji house bowed to the Shimazu, with [[p:鍋島直茂|Nabeshima Naoshige]] holding it together.

terms.ja: 秀吉は織田信雄と単独で和を結び、戦う名分を失った家康も兵を引いた。家康は次男の於義丸 (結城秀康) を秀吉の養子として送った。
terms.en: Hideyoshi made a separate peace with Oda Nobukatsu, and Ieyasu, his cause gone, withdrew too. He sent his second son Ogimaru (Yūki Hideyasu) to be Hideyoshi's adopted son.

name.ja: 佐竹・蘆名連合の伊達攻め
name.en: the Satake and Ashina allies' war on Date

terms.ja: 連合軍は国へ引き揚げ、二本松の畠山は孤立した。
terms.en: The allies went home, and the Hatakeyama of Nihonmatsu were left alone.
