legend:フロイス『日欧文化比較』|Fróis, Tratado

body.ja:
馬廻 (うままわり) とは、大将の馬のまわりを固める侍のことである。合戦では本陣を守り、伝令に走り、ここぞというときに大将とともに突き進む。ふだんは城下に住み、主君のそばに仕えた。

領地を持つ重臣は、自分の家臣を率いて戦う。その兵は重臣のものである。これに対して馬廻は、大名が自分で抱える兵であった。馬廻を厚くすることは、大名が重臣に頼らない力を持つことを意味した。

[[p:織田信長]]は若い頃から、家の次男や三男を集めて身近に置いた。そのうち選り抜きの者に赤と黒の母衣 (ほろ) を背負わせたのが、赤母衣衆と黒母衣衆である。母衣は竹の骨に布を張った大きな袋で、馬を走らせると風をはらんでふくらみ、遠くからも見分けがつく。[[p:前田利家]]は赤母衣衆、佐々成政は黒母衣衆の筆頭であった。1560年の桶狭間で、信長が清洲を飛び出したとき従ったのは、主従わずか六騎であったという。熱田で追いついた兵を合わせても二千ほど。その中心が馬廻であった。

信長は1576年に安土に城を築くと、馬廻と弓衆に城下へ移り住むよう命じた。1578年、弓衆の家から火が出たとき、信長は妻子を尾張に残したままの者が百二十人いるのを知り、尾張の家を焼かせて妻子を安土へ移らせた。兵を土地から切り離して城下に集めるやり方は、こうして進められた。

豊臣秀吉の馬廻は「七手組」と呼ばれ、七人の組頭がそれぞれ千人ほどを率いて大坂城を守った。[[p:徳川家康]]の馬廻は「旗本」と呼ばれる。旗の本、つまり本陣を守る者の意である。江戸時代になると、旗本は将軍に直接仕える家臣の名となった。
body.en:
The umamawari, "those about the horse", were the samurai who kept close round the commander's mount. In battle they guarded the headquarters, carried orders, and at the decisive moment went forward with the commander himself. In peace they lived below the castle and served at their lord's side.

A great vassal with lands of his own led his own men to war, and those men were his. The horse guards were the lord's own. To strengthen them was to have a force that did not depend on the great vassals.

From his youth [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]] gathered younger sons of good families about him. The pick of them wore a red or a black horo on their backs: the Red Horo and the Black Horo. A horo is a great bag of cloth on a bamboo frame that fills with wind at a gallop and can be made out from far off. [[p:前田利家|Maeda Toshiie]] headed the Red, Sassa Narimasa the Black. At Okehazama in 1560, when Nobunaga rode out of Kiyosu, only six horsemen, master and men, are said to have followed; with those who caught up at Atsuta there were some two thousand. The horse guards were their core.

When Nobunaga built Azuchi in 1576 he ordered his horse guards and archers to move below the castle. In 1578, when fire broke out in an archer's house, he found that a hundred and twenty of them had left wives and children behind in Owari; he had their Owari houses burned and their families brought to Azuchi. That was how soldiers were cut loose from the land and gathered under the castle.

Toyotomi Hideyoshi's horse guards were the "seven companies", seven captains each with about a thousand men, who garrisoned Osaka castle. [[p:徳川家康|Tokugawa Ieyasu]]'s were called hatamoto — "at the foot of the banner", those who guard the headquarters. In the Edo period hatamoto became the name of the shogun's direct retainers.

title.ja: 城攻めの手立て (仕寄・付城・金掘り)

body.ja:
戦国の日本には、数万とも言われる城があった。山の尾根を削って堀と土塁をめぐらせた山城である。野での合戦よりも、城を囲む戦いのほうがはるかに多かった。

力で攻めるのを「力攻め」という。堀を越え、塀に取り付く。攻め手は「仕寄 (しより)」を進めた。竹を束ねて鉄砲の弾を防ぐ「竹束」を押し立て、その陰で土を掘り、少しずつ城に近づく。高い櫓「井楼」を組んで、上から城内へ撃ちかける。力攻めは損害が大きく、大名はできるだけ避けた。

多く使われたのは「兵糧攻め」である。城のまわりに「付城」をいくつも築いて道を断ち、食べ物が尽きるのを待つ。[[p:羽柴秀吉]]はこれを得意とした。1578年からの播磨の三木城は二年近く囲まれて落ち、「三木の干殺し」と呼ばれた。1581年の因幡の鳥取城では、秀吉はあらかじめ商人に命じて国じゅうの米を高値で買い占めさせ、さらに村々を襲って百姓を城へ追い込んだ。城は四か月で落ちた。『信長公記』は、餓えた人々が柵にすがって助けを求め、鉄砲で撃たれた者に人が群がったと記す。

水も使われた。1582年、秀吉は備中の高松城のまわりに長い堤を築いて足守川の水を引き入れ、城を湖の中に沈めた。1590年の武蔵の忍城でも同じ手が試みられている。

山を掘る者たちもいた。甲斐の武田家は金山で働く「金掘り衆」を抱えていた。1571年の駿河の深沢城では金掘り衆が本丸の近くまで掘り進み、1573年の三河の野田城では井戸の水の筋を掘り抜いて水を断ち、城を開かせた。

1590年、秀吉は二十万を超える兵で小田原城を囲み、城を見下ろす山の上に、石垣と天守を持つ城を八十日ほどで築いた。出来上がるとまわりの木をいっせいに切り払わせたので、城の中からは一夜で現れたように見えたという。小田原は三か月で開いた。
body.en:
Sengoku Japan had tens of thousands of castles, it is said: hill castles, the ridges cut into ditches and earth banks. Far more of the fighting was round castles than in open battle.

To take one by force was a "storming": cross the ditches and get onto the palisades. The attackers pushed forward their approaches — bundles of bamboo set up to stop bullets, with men digging forward behind them — and built tall scaffold towers to shoot down into the castle. Storming was costly, and the lords avoided it when they could.

The common way was to starve a castle out: ring it with forts of one's own to cut every road, and wait. [[p:羽柴秀吉|Hashiba Hideyoshi]] was a master of it. Miki castle in Harima, invested from 1578, fell after nearly two years — "the starving of Miki". At Tottori in Inaba in 1581 he had merchants buy up the province's rice beforehand at high prices and then raided the villages to drive the peasants into the castle. It fell in four months. The Chronicle of Nobunaga tells of the starving clinging to the palisade and begging, and of people swarming on those the guns had brought down.

Water was used too. In 1582 Hideyoshi built a long dyke round Takamatsu castle in Bitchū, turned the Ashimori river into it and left the castle standing in a lake. The same was tried at Oshi in Musashi in 1590.

And there were men who dug. The Takeda of Kai kept miners from their gold mines. At Fukasawa in Suruga in 1571 they dug close under the main enclosure; at Noda in Mikawa in 1573 they cut through to the veins of the well, took away the water, and the castle opened.

In 1590 Hideyoshi surrounded Odawara with more than two hundred thousand men and, on a hill looking down into it, built in some eighty days a castle with stone walls and a keep. When it was done he had the trees around it felled all at once, so that from inside Odawara it seemed to have appeared overnight. Odawara opened its gates in three months.

body.ja:
15世紀の半ば、本願寺の蓮如は教えをやさしい言葉の手紙に書いて各地へ送り、村ごとに寄り合いを作らせた。百姓も商人も職人も侍も、同じ教えを信じる者として対等に結ばれる。こうして結ばれた人々を門徒という。門徒が力を合わせて立ち上がることを「一向一揆」と呼んだ。

1488年、加賀の門徒は守護の富樫政親を高尾城に攻めて滅ぼした。それから九十年あまり、加賀は門徒と寺が治める国となる。人はこれを「百姓の持ちたる国のよう」と書いた。

門徒の強さは数と結びつきにあった。寺を中心に堀と土塁で囲んだ「寺内町」を築き、商いで富み、鉄砲を買い集めた。大坂の石山本願寺は、川と海に守られた大きな寺内町であった。

1570年の九月、[[p:織田信長]]が三好勢を攻めていたさなか、本願寺の[[p:顕如]]は門徒に立ち上がるよう呼びかけ、夜のうちに鐘を鳴らして織田の陣を襲わせた。ここから十年に及ぶ石山合戦が始まる。同じ年の十一月、伊勢の長島の門徒が立ち、信長の弟の信興を小木江城に攻めて自害させた。

信長は長島を三度攻めた。1571年と1573年は退くところを襲われて大きな損害を出した。1574年、信長は海と川を船で埋めて長島を囲み、兵糧を断った。降ると言って出て来た者も撃たせ、最後に残った二万人を柵で囲んで四方から火を放った。越前では1575年、府中の町が死体で埋まり、信長は「空き所なく」と手紙に書いた。

石山は落ちなかった。毛利の水軍が海から兵糧を運び、雑賀の鉄砲衆が城を守った。1580年、天皇の仲立ちで和が結ばれ、顕如は石山を出た。加賀の門徒も同じ年に[[p:柴田勝家]]に敗れた。門徒衆は大名の軍ではなかったが、信長を最も長く苦しめた相手であった。
body.en:
In the middle of the fifteenth century Rennyo of the Honganji put his teaching into letters in plain words, sent them round the country and had the villages form their own gatherings. Farmer, merchant, craftsman and samurai who held the same teaching were bound together as equals. People so bound were monto, the adherents; and when they rose together it was called an ikkō ikki.

In 1488 the adherents of Kaga attacked their military governor, Togashi Masachika, in Takao castle and destroyed him. For more than ninety years Kaga was a province run by the believers and their temples — "like a province held by the peasants", as it was written.

Their strength was numbers and solidarity. They built temple towns ringed with ditch and bank, grew rich on trade and bought guns. The Ishiyama Honganji at Osaka was a great temple town, guarded by rivers and the sea.

In the ninth month of 1570, while [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]] was attacking the Miyoshi, [[p:顕如|Kennyo]] of the Honganji called on the adherents to rise, and had the bell rung in the night and Nobunaga's camp attacked. So began the ten-year Ishiyama war. In the eleventh month of that year the believers of Nagashima in Ise rose, attacked Nobunaga's brother Nobuoki in Kokie castle and drove him to take his own life.

Nobunaga attacked Nagashima three times. In 1571 and 1573 he was caught as he withdrew and lost heavily. In 1574 he filled river and sea with boats, ringed Nagashima and cut off its food. Those who came out offering to surrender were shot; the last twenty thousand were fenced in and burned from all sides. In Echizen in 1575 the town of Fuchū was choked with the dead — "no empty ground left", Nobunaga wrote in a letter.

Ishiyama did not fall. The Mōri navy brought food in by sea and the gunners of Saika held the walls. In 1580 peace was made through the emperor's good offices and Kennyo left Ishiyama; the believers of Kaga were beaten by [[p:柴田勝家|Shibata Katsuie]] the same year. The leagues were no lord's army, and yet no enemy gave Nobunaga trouble for so long.

title.en: The sea lords and their fleets

body.ja:
瀬戸内海は、畿内と九州、さらに朝鮮と明を結ぶ海の道である。島が多く、潮の流れが速く、狭い瀬戸を知らない船は進めない。この海を押さえていたのが「海賊衆」であった。

海賊といっても、ただの盗賊ではない。彼らは海の関所を構え、通る船から「帆別銭」「駄別料」と呼ばれる通行料を取った。払った船には水先案内を付け、ほかの海賊から守った。最も大きかったのが、伊予の能島・来島と備後の因島に本拠を置いた三つの村上氏である。宣教師フロイスは能島の[[p:村上武吉]]を「日本最大の海賊」と書き、その紋の入った旗を掲げていれば襲われない、と記している。

船は三つの型に分けられる。安宅船 (あたけぶね) は櫓を五十挺から百挺以上備え、厚い板の楯で囲んだ大船で、数十人から百人以上の兵を載せる。関船は櫓四十挺ほどの中型の速い船。小早は櫓十数挺の小舟で、物見と伝令、火攻めに使った。

武器は弓と鉄砲、そして「焙烙 (ほうろく)」である。素焼きの丸い器に火薬を詰め、火を付けて敵の船に投げ込む。1576年の第一次木津川口の戦いで、毛利方の水軍はこの焙烙と火矢で織田方の船を焼き払った。

大名はみな海の兵を求めた。毛利は村上氏と小早川の水軍を、織田は志摩の[[p:九鬼嘉隆]]を、北条は伊豆と相模の海賊衆を、里見は安房の水軍を抱えた。1555年の厳島の戦いで[[p:毛利元就]]が陶晴賢を破ったとき、勝ち負けを決めたのは来島の村上氏が毛利に付いたことであったと伝わる。

1588年、豊臣秀吉は刀狩と同じ日に「海賊停止令」を出した。海の上で通行料を取ることを禁じ、海賊衆に大名の家臣になるか、百姓になるかを選ばせた。海の自由な領主たちはこれで姿を消し、水軍は大名の船手組となって朝鮮へ渡ることになる。
body.en:
The Inland Sea is the sea road between the home provinces and Kyushu, and on to Korea and Ming China: full of islands, with racing tides and narrow straits no stranger could pass. The men who held it were the kaizoku-shū, the "pirate bands".

They were not mere robbers. They kept barriers on the sea and took tolls from passing ships; a ship that paid got a pilot and protection from other pirates. The greatest were the three Murakami houses, of Noshima and Kurushima in Iyo and Innoshima in Bingo. The missionary Fróis called [[p:村上武吉|Murakami Takeyoshi]] of Noshima "the greatest pirate in Japan", and noted that a ship flying a flag with his crest would not be attacked.

There were three kinds of ship. The atakebune was a great vessel of fifty to over a hundred oars, walled with thick plank shields, carrying dozens to over a hundred fighting men. The sekibune was a fast middle-sized ship of about forty oars. The kobaya was a small boat of a dozen oars or so, for scouting, messages and fire attacks.

They fought with bow and gun, and with the hōroku: a round unglazed pot packed with powder, lit and thrown into an enemy ship. At the first battle of the Kizu river mouth in 1576 the Mōri navy burned the Oda fleet with these and with fire arrows.

Every lord wanted men of the sea. The Mōri had the Murakami and the Kobayakawa fleet, the Oda had [[p:九鬼嘉隆|Kuki Yoshitaka]] of Shima, the Hōjō the pirate bands of Izu and Sagami, the Satomi the fleet of Awa. When [[p:毛利元就|Mōri Motonari]] beat Sue Harukata at Itsukushima in 1555, what decided it, tradition says, was the Murakami of Kurushima coming over to him.

In 1588, on the same day as the sword hunt, Toyotomi Hideyoshi issued his ban on piracy. Tolls at sea were forbidden, and the pirate bands had to choose between becoming a lord's vassals and becoming farmers. The free lords of the sea were gone; the fleets became the lords' ship companies, and went to Korea.

src: legend:フロイス『日本史』|Fróis, History of Japan

title.en: Shinobi: the men of Iga and Kōka

body.ja:
敵の城に忍び入り、様子を探り、火を付け、夜襲の手引きをする者を「忍び」という。国によって呼び名は違い、「透波 (すっぱ)」「乱波 (らっぱ)」「草」「かまり」とも呼ばれた。

名高いのは近江の甲賀と伊賀の者たちである。どちらも山に囲まれ、大きな大名がおらず、小さな土豪たちが寄り合って国を治めていた。伊賀の土豪たちは掟を定め、他国の兵が入ればみなで防ぐこと、十七歳から五十歳までの者は残らず出ること、他国の者を引き入れた者は罰することを取り決めている。「惣国一揆」と呼ばれる仕組みである。

1487年、将軍の足利義尚が近江の六角高頼を攻めたとき、高頼は甲賀の山へ逃げ込んだ。甲賀の者たちは将軍の陣を夜ごとに襲い、霧や煙にまぎれて火を放ったという。将軍は陣中で病死した。甲賀の名が広く知られたのは、この「鈎 (まがり) の陣」からである。

確かな記録もある。1541年、大和の笠置城に伊賀の者たちが忍び入り、坊舎に火を放って城の一部を奪った。奈良の僧の日記は「伊賀衆忍び入る」と書いている。彼らは雇われて働く、山城の夜襲の専門家であった。

1579年、[[p:織田信長]]の子の信雄は父に無断で伊賀に攻め入り、山の中で伏兵に襲われて大敗した。信長は激怒した。1581年、信長は四万を超える兵を六つの口から入れ、村も寺も焼き払った。伊賀の惣国はここで滅んだ。

翌年、本能寺の変が起こったとき、[[p:徳川家康]]は堺にいた。わずかな供と伊賀の山を越えて三河へ逃げ帰るとき、伊賀と甲賀の者たちが道を守ったという。家康はのちに彼ら二百人を召し抱え、[[p:服部半蔵]]に預けた。江戸城の門の一つは今も「半蔵門」と呼ばれる。黒い装束で手裏剣を投げる「忍者」の姿は、ずっと後の芝居と読み物が作ったものである。
body.en:
Those who stole into an enemy castle, spied out how things stood, set fires and guided night attacks were shinobi. The name differed from province to province: suppa, rappa, kusa, kamari.

The famous ones were the men of Kōka in Ōmi and of Iga. Both were hill countries with no great lord, run by leagues of small landholders. Those of Iga drew up rules: if another province's troops came in, all would resist; every man from seventeen to fifty would turn out; anyone who let outsiders in would be punished. It was called the league of the whole province.

In 1487, when the shogun Ashikaga Yoshihisa attacked Rokkaku Takayori of Ōmi, Takayori fled into the hills of Kōka. The men of Kōka raided the shogun's camp night after night, it is said, setting fires under cover of mist and smoke; the shogun died of sickness in camp. From this "camp at Magari" the name of Kōka became known.

There is firm record too. In 1541 men of Iga stole into Kasagi castle in Yamato, set fire to the priests' quarters and took part of it; a Nara monk's diary says simply, "the Iga band stole in." They were specialists for hire in night attacks on hill castles.

In 1579 Nobukatsu, a son of [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]], invaded Iga without his father's leave, was ambushed in the hills and badly beaten. Nobunaga was furious. In 1581 he sent more than forty thousand men in by six roads and burned villages and temples alike. The league of Iga ended there.

The next year, when Nobunaga was killed at Honnōji, [[p:徳川家康|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] was at Sakai. As he fled home to Mikawa over the hills of Iga with a handful of followers, men of Iga and Kōka are said to have guarded the road. He later took two hundred of them into service under [[p:服部半蔵|Hattori Hanzō]]; a gate of Edo castle is still called the Hanzō gate. The black-clad "ninja" throwing star-shaped blades is the creation of plays and storybooks of a much later time.

src: legend:伊賀惣国一揆掟書|the rules of the Iga league

body.ja:
鉄砲を大きくしたものを「大筒 (おおづつ)」、ヨーロッパから来た大砲を「石火矢 (いしびや)」という。戦国の日本で大砲は長く脇役であった。山城は土でできており、道は細く、重い砲を運ぶのは難しい。鉄砲のほうがはるかに役に立った。

最初に大砲を手に入れたのは豊後の[[p:大友宗麟]]である。1576年、宗麟はポルトガル人から大砲を受け取った。砲身の後ろに、火薬と弾を詰めた取り外しのできる筒を差し込んで撃つ仕組みで、ポルトガル人が船に載せていたものである。宗麟はこれを「国崩し」と名付けた。1586年、島津の大軍が臼杵の丹生島城に攻め寄せたとき、この国崩しが火を噴き、島津の兵は驚いて退いたという。

国内でも作られた。近江の国友と和泉の堺の鉄砲鍛冶は、鉄砲と同じように鉄の板を巻いて鍛え、口径の大きな筒を作った。数十匁から一貫目 (約三・七五キログラム) の弾を撃つ。[[p:織田信長]]が[[p:九鬼嘉隆]]に造らせた大船にも大筒が載せられ、1578年の木津川口で毛利の船を撃ち砕いた。

大砲が戦の行方を決めたのは、1614年の大坂冬の陣である。[[p:徳川家康]]は国友と堺に大筒を作らせ、さらにイギリスとオランダの商館から大砲を買い入れた。イギリスから買ったのはカルバリン砲四門とセーカー砲一門である。砲は大坂城の北と東から昼も夜も撃ち込まれた。弾の一つが本丸の御殿に当たり、[[p:淀殿]]の侍女たちが死んだ。城方は和議に応じた。

家康が攻め落とせなかった城を開かせたのは、堀を越えて届く砲の音と弾であった。だがこの戦いののち二百年あまり、日本では大きな戦がなくなり、大砲の技はほとんど進まなかった。
body.en:
A matchlock made large was an ōzutsu, a "great tube"; the cannon that came from Europe was an ishibiya, a "stone fire-arrow". In Sengoku Japan cannon were long a sideshow: hill castles were made of earth, roads were narrow, heavy guns were hard to move, and the matchlock was far more useful.

The first to get cannon was [[p:大友宗麟|Ōtomo Sōrin]] of Bungo. In 1576 he received guns from the Portuguese — breech-loaders of the kind they carried on their ships, fired with a removable chamber of powder and shot wedged in behind the barrel. He named one "Destroyer of Provinces". In 1586, when the great Shimazu army came up to his castle of Nyūjima at Usuki, it opened fire, and the Shimazu men, it is said, fell back in alarm.

They were made at home too. The gunsmiths of Kunitomo in Ōmi and Sakai in Izumi forged large-bore pieces as they forged matchlocks, from wrapped iron plate, throwing shot from a few ounces to nearly four kilograms. The great ships [[p:九鬼嘉隆|Kuki Yoshitaka]] built for [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]] carried such guns, and shattered Mōri ships at the Kizu river mouth in 1578.

Cannon decided a campaign in the winter siege of Osaka in 1614. [[p:徳川家康|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] had great guns made at Kunitomo and Sakai and bought cannon from the English and Dutch factories — from the English, four culverins and a saker. They fired into the castle from north and east by day and night. One shot hit the residence in the main enclosure and killed ladies-in-waiting of [[p:淀殿|Lady Yodo]]. The defenders agreed to terms.

What opened a castle Ieyasu could not storm was the noise and the shot of guns that reached across its moats. But after that war Japan had no great war for more than two hundred years, and the gunner's art hardly advanced.

src: legend:フロイス『日本史』|Fróis, History of Japan
legend:イギリス商館長日記|the diary of the English factory

body.ja:
中世の大きな寺は、広い荘園を持つ領主であった。領地を守り、年貢を集め、ほかの寺や武士と争うために、寺は武装した者たちを抱えた。頭を布で包み、高下駄を履き、薙刀を持つ姿で知られる。彼らを「衆徒 (しゅと)」「堂衆」「行人」などと呼ぶ。「僧兵」は後の時代の呼び方である。

大和の国は特別であった。奈良の興福寺が国じゅうの土地を押さえ、鎌倉にも室町にも幕府は大和に守護を置けなかった。興福寺のもとで実際に兵を率いたのが、寺に属する在地の武士たちである。筒井家はその筆頭で、興福寺の衆徒の頭 (官符衆徒) であった。[[p:筒井順慶]]は僧の姿をした大名である。

興福寺の僧の胤栄は、十文字の穂先を持つ槍の術を編み出した。「宝蔵院流」と呼ばれ、江戸時代を通じて最も広まった槍の流派となる。

紀伊の根来寺は、数千の「行人」を抱える大きな寺であった。寺の者が種子島から鉄砲を持ち帰り、門前の鍛冶に作らせたと伝わる。根来の鉄砲衆は雑賀衆と並んで名高く、雇われて各地で戦った。宣教師たちは、彼らが長い髪を背に垂らし、毎日鉄砲を撃つ稽古をしていると書いている。

近江の比叡山延暦寺は、京の鬼門を守る寺として朝廷も手を出せない力を持っていた。1570年、浅井・朝倉の軍が比叡山に逃げ込むと、[[p:織田信長]]は寺に「味方をするか、せめてどちらにも付くな」と求めた。寺は答えなかった。翌年の九月、信長は山を囲んで火を放ち、堂も塔も焼き払った。『信長公記』は、僧も稚児も学僧も、逃げ場を失った者は一人残らず首をはねられたと記す。

根来寺は1585年に豊臣秀吉に焼かれ、興福寺は秀吉の弟の秀長が大和に入ると領地を削られた。寺が兵を持つ時代はここで終わった。
body.en:
The great temples of medieval Japan were lords of wide estates. To guard their lands, gather their dues and fight other temples and warriors, they kept armed men — known by the cloth-wrapped head, the high clogs and the glaive. They were called shuto, dōshu, gyōnin; "warrior monk" is a later word.

Yamato was a province apart. The Kōfukuji of Nara held its land, and neither shogunate ever set a military governor over it. The men who actually led troops under the Kōfukuji were the local warriors attached to it, and first among them the Tsutsui, heads of the temple's shuto. [[p:筒井順慶|Tsutsui Junkei]] was a lord in a monk's habit.

In'ei, a monk of the Kōfukuji, devised a way of fighting with a cross-bladed spear. As the Hōzōin school it became the most widespread school of the spear through the Edo period.

The Negoroji in Kii was a great temple with several thousand gyōnin. One of its men, tradition says, brought a gun back from Tanegashima and had the smiths at the temple gate copy it. The gunners of Negoro were as famous as those of Saika and fought for hire across the country; the missionaries write of their long hair hanging down their backs and their daily practice at the mark.

The Enryakuji on Mount Hiei, guardian of the capital's unlucky quarter, had a power the court itself dared not touch. In 1570, when the armies of Azai and Asakura took refuge on the mountain, [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]] asked the temple to take his side, or at least neither. It gave no answer. In the ninth month of the next year he ringed the mountain and set it alight, halls and pagodas together. The Chronicle of Nobunaga says that priests, boys and scholars, whoever could not get away, were beheaded to the last one.

The Negoroji was burned by Toyotomi Hideyoshi in 1585, and the Kōfukuji lost its lands when Hideyoshi's brother Hidenaga came into Yamato. The age of temples with soldiers ended there.

src: legend:フロイス『日本史』|Fróis, History of Japan

body.ja:
土佐は山が九割を占め、平地は少ない。[[p:長宗我部元親]]は、この貧しい国から四国をほぼ手に入れた。その軍を支えたのが「一領具足 (いちりょうぐそく)」である。

一領具足は、ふだんは自分の田を耕す半農の武士である。持っている具足 (よろい) はただ一領、替えはない。馬も乗り替えがない。それでこう呼ばれた。

後の『土佐物語』は、その姿をこう伝える。田に出るときも、槍の柄に具足と兵糧をくくり付けて畦に突き立てておく。「それ」と声がかかれば、鎌も鍬も放り出して、そのまま戦場へ駆け出す。日ごろから武勇だけを心がけ、命を塵ほどにも思わず、礼儀や作法は知らない。

彼らは強かった。自分の田を守るために戦い、戦えば田が増える。元親は1575年に土佐を一つにまとめ、阿波・讃岐・伊予へ兵を進め、1585年には四国の大半を従えた。

だが弱みもあった。田植えと稲刈りの季節には兵を出せず、遠くへ長く出ることもできない。武具は古く、鉄砲は少ない。1585年、豊臣秀吉が十万を超える兵を四国へ送ると、元親の家臣の谷忠澄は言った。「上方の兵は武具も馬も光り輝き、兵糧も十分です。こちらは十人のうち七人は小さな土佐駒に乗り、鞍は曲がり、具足の糸は麻で綴ってあります。国は長い戦で疲れ、とても太刀打ちできません。」元親は降り、土佐一国だけを許された。

1600年の関ヶ原ののち長宗我部家が領地を失うと、一領具足たちは浦戸城の明け渡しを拒んで立てこもった。新しい領主の山内家は彼らを欺いて討ち、二百七十三の首が大坂へ送られた。生き残った者たちは「郷士」として低い身分に置かれた。二百六十年ののち、土佐の郷士の中から幕府を倒す者たちが出ることになる。
body.en:
Tosa is nine parts mountain and has little flat land. From that poor province [[p:長宗我部元親|Chōsokabe Motochika]] won nearly all of Shikoku. His army stood on the ichiryō gusoku, the "one-suit men".

They were half farmer, half warrior, working their own fields in ordinary times. They owned one suit of armour and no spare, one horse and no remount: hence the name.

The later Tale of Tosa describes them. Even going out to the fields a man tied his armour and rations to his spear shaft and stuck it in the bank. At the call he dropped sickle and hoe and ran straight off to war. They thought of nothing but valour, held life as light as dust, and knew nothing of manners.

They were formidable: they fought for their own fields, and fighting brought them more. Motochika united Tosa in 1575, pushed into Awa, Sanuki and Iyo, and by 1585 held most of Shikoku.

They had weaknesses too. They could not march at planting or harvest, nor far, nor for long. Their gear was old and their guns few. In 1585, when Toyotomi Hideyoshi sent more than a hundred thousand men into Shikoku, Motochika's retainer Tani Tadazumi told him: "The soldiers of the capital region shine, arms and horses, and have food in plenty. Seven in ten of ours ride little Tosa ponies with warped saddles, and their armour is laced with hemp. The province is worn out with long war. We cannot match them." Motochika submitted, and was left Tosa alone.

When the Chōsokabe lost their lands after Sekigahara in 1600, the one-suit men refused to hand over Urado castle and shut themselves in it. The new lords, the Yamauchi, tricked and killed them, and two hundred and seventy-three heads went to Osaka. The survivors were kept down as "country samurai". Two hundred and sixty years later, men from among the country samurai of Tosa would help bring down the shogunate.

body.ja:
室町の将軍には、自分に直接仕える武士の一団があった。奉公衆 (ほうこうしゅう) である。五つの番に分かれ、交代で御所を守り、将軍が出かけるときは供をした。合わせて三百人から三百五十人ほど。全国の有力な武士の家から選ばれ、それぞれの国にある領地は守護の手が及ばないものとされた。

将軍は守護大名たちの上に立っていたが、自分の兵は少ない。奉公衆は、その将軍が自分で動かせるただ一つの力であった。1487年に足利義尚が近江の六角を攻めたとき、中心となったのは奉公衆である。

1493年、管領の細川政元が将軍を取り替えると (明応の政変)、奉公衆は二つに割れ、多くが将軍のもとを去った。以後の将軍は、細川や三好や六角など、そのときどきの有力者に担がれなければ京にいることもできなくなった。

1565年の五月、[[p:三好義継]]と松永久通らの一万の兵が、訴えがあると言って将軍[[p:足利義輝]]の御所を囲んだ。御所にいたのは奉公衆ら数十人であった。義輝は剣術を塚原卜伝に学んだ使い手である。足利家に伝わる名刀を何本も畳に突き立て、刃がこぼれるたびに取り替えて斬り結んだ、と後の軍記は語る。奉公衆はことごとく討死し、義輝も果てた。

弟の義昭は[[p:細川藤孝]]ら奉公衆に助けられて奈良を逃れ、[[p:織田信長]]に担がれて1568年に京へ戻った。だが義昭が信長と争って1573年に京を追われると、奉公衆の多くは信長に仕え、あるいは義昭に従って備後の鞆へ落ちた。[[p:明智光秀]]も細川藤孝も、もとはこの将軍のそばにいた者たちである。
body.en:
The Muromachi shoguns had a body of warriors serving them directly: the hōkōshū. They were in five watches, guarding the palace by turns and escorting the shogun when he went out — three hundred to three hundred and fifty men in all, chosen from leading warrior houses across the country, their lands in the provinces held to be beyond the reach of the military governors.

The shogun stood above the governor-lords but had few troops of his own. The hōkōshū were the one force he could move himself. When Ashikaga Yoshihisa attacked the Rokkaku of Ōmi in 1487, they were its core.

In 1493, when the deputy Hosokawa Masamoto replaced one shogun with another, the hōkōshū split and many left the shogun's service. From then on a shogun could not even stay in Kyoto unless some strong man of the day — Hosokawa, Miyoshi, Rokkaku — carried him.

In the fifth month of 1565 ten thousand men under [[p:三好義継|Miyoshi Yoshitsugu]] and [[p:まつ|Matsu]]naga Hisamichi, claiming to bring a petition, surrounded the palace of the shogun [[p:足利義輝|Ashikaga Yoshiteru]]. A few dozen men of the guard were inside. Yoshiteru was a swordsman, a pupil of Tsukahara Bokuden. He stuck the famous blades of the Ashikaga house upright in the matting, the later war tales say, and took a fresh one each time an edge was notched. The guard died to a man, and Yoshiteru with them.

His brother Yoshiaki got out of Nara with the help of [[p:細川藤孝|Hosokawa Fujitaka]] and others of the guard, and came back to Kyoto in 1568 carried by [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]]. When he fell out with Nobunaga and was driven from the capital in 1573, most of the guard took service with Nobunaga, or followed Yoshiaki to Tomo in Bingo. [[p:明智光秀|Akechi Mitsuhide]] and Hosokawa Fujitaka had both begun at this shogun's side.

src: legend:フロイス『日本史』|Fróis, History of Japan

body.ja:
主を失った武士を牢人 (ろうにん) という。1600年の関ヶ原ののち、[[p:徳川家康]]は西軍に付いた大名八十八家の領地を取り上げ、五家を大きく削った。その家臣たちは仕える先を失った。数は数十万とも言われる。

新しく召し抱えられる者は少なかった。戦がなければ兵は要らない。大名は、もとの主の敵に仕えた者を雇うのをためらった。牢人たちは京や大坂の町に流れ込み、寺子屋の師匠や用心棒、日雇いをして暮らした。

1614年、徳川と豊臣の間が破れると、大坂城は金と銀を出して牢人を募った。集まった者は十万ほど。豊臣に恩のある大名は一人も来なかったが、名のある牢人が来た。信濃の上田で二度まで徳川を退けた[[p:真田昌幸]]の子の信繁。黒田家を飛び出した[[p:後藤又兵衛]]。土佐を失った[[p:長宗我部盛親]]。豊前小倉の領地を失った毛利勝永。宇喜多家の家老であった明石全登。この五人が「五人衆」と呼ばれる。

牢人たちにとって、これは最後の機会であった。勝てば領地が戻る。負ければ何も残らない。[[p:真田信繁]]は城の南に出丸を築き、押し寄せた徳川方に大きな損害を与えた。

いったん和が結ばれ、堀が埋められると、徳川は牢人を城から出すよう求めた。行く先のない牢人たちは去らなかった。1615年の五月、堀を失った大坂方は城を出て戦うほかなかった。後藤又兵衛は道明寺で、長宗我部盛親は八尾で戦い、最後の日、毛利勝永と真田信繁は天王寺口から家康の本陣めがけて突き進んだ。家康の馬印が倒れ、家康は三里も逃げたという。信繁は力尽きて討たれ、城は燃え落ちた。

戦のあと、徳川は逃げた牢人を厳しく捜した。牢人の問題はそれでも片づかず、1651年には軍学者の由井正雪が牢人を集めて幕府を倒そうとする事件が起こっている。
body.en:
A warrior who had lost his lord was a rōnin. After Sekigahara in 1600 [[p:徳川家康|Tokugawa Ieyasu]] took the lands of eighty-eight lords who had sided with the west and cut down five more. Their retainers had no one left to serve — hundreds of thousands of them, by some counts.

Few found new masters. Without war no one needs soldiers, and a lord thought twice before hiring men who had served his old enemy. The rōnin drifted into Kyoto and Osaka and lived as teachers, hired guards and day labourers.

In 1614, when Tokugawa and Toyotomi broke, Osaka castle laid out its gold and silver for rōnin. About a hundred thousand came. Not one lord who owed the Toyotomi a debt joined them; but famous rōnin did. [[p:真田信繁|Sanada Nobushige]], son of the Masayuki who had twice thrown the Tokugawa back from Ueda in Shinano. [[p:後藤又兵衛|Gotō Matabei]], who had walked out of the Kuroda house. [[p:長宗我部盛親|Chōsokabe Morichika]], who had lost Tosa. Mōri Katsunaga, who had lost Kokura in Buzen. Akashi Takenori, once an elder of the Ukita. These were the "five".

For the rōnin it was the last chance. Win, and their lands came back; lose, and nothing was left. Nobushige built an outwork south of the castle and made the Tokugawa pay heavily for coming at it.

When peace was patched up and the moats were filled, the Tokugawa demanded that the rōnin be sent away. Men with nowhere to go did not leave. In the fifth month of 1615, without its moats, Osaka could only come out and fight. Gotō Matabei fought at Dōmyōji and Chōsokabe Morichika at Yao; on the last day Mōri Katsunaga and Sanada Nobushige drove from the Tennōji approach straight at Ieyasu's headquarters. His standard went down and he fled, it is said, three leagues. Nobushige, spent, was killed, and the castle burned.

After the war the Tokugawa hunted the fugitives hard. The problem of the rōnin did not go away: in 1651 the military scholar Yui Shōsetsu gathered rōnin in a plot to overthrow the shogunate.

src: legend:大坂御陣覚書|the Osaka campaign memoranda

title.ja: 鉄砲はどの家に多かったか

body.ja:
1543年、種子島に流れ着いた船のポルトガル人が、火縄で撃つ鉄の筒を持っていた。島の主の種子島時堯は二挺を買い取り、刀鍛冶に同じものを作らせた。作り方は紀伊の根来、和泉の堺、近江の国友へと伝わる。それから戦場に広がるまで、家によって二十年以上の開きがあった。

早かったのは西と畿内である。戦で鉄砲を使った最も古い記録は1549年、薩摩の[[p:島津貴久]]が大隅の加治木を攻めたときのものとされる。翌1550年には京の東山で、三好方の兵が鉄砲に当たって死んだと公家の日記にある。1553年、[[p:織田信長]]が舅の斎藤道三と会ったとき、供の行列には弓と鉄砲あわせて五百挺が並んでいた。

東にも届いた。1555年、[[p:武田信玄]]は信濃の旭山城に弓八百張と鉄砲三百挺を送り込んでいる。1559年に京へ上った長尾景虎 ([[p:上杉謙信]]) は、将軍[[p:足利義輝]]から火薬の調合の仕方を記した書き付けを授かった。

だが数には差があった。残っている軍役の帳面を比べると、上杉家は1575年に五千五百余りのうち鉄砲三百十六挺で、およそ十七人に一人。北条家の岩付の衆は1577年に千五百八十のうち五十挺余りで、三十人に一人しかいない。土佐の長宗我部家の兵は、豊臣の軍に比べて武具が古く鉄砲が少ないと、自分たちの家臣が認めている。

差を生んだのは弾と火薬である。火薬に要る硝石は日本ではほとんど採れず、明や東南アジアから船で運ばれた。入り口は堺と九州の港である。1567年、[[p:大友宗麟]]はマカオの司教に手紙を送り、良い硝石を毎年自分だけに売り、敵の毛利には売らないでほしいと頼んだ。武田信玄は家臣に「長柄の槍を減らしてでも鉄砲を持て」と命じたが、甲斐は海から遠く、弾と火薬はいつも足りなかった。

1575年の長篠で、織田信長が五人の奉行に預けて柵の内に並べた鉄砲は「千挺ばかり」と『信長公記』は書く。有名な「三千挺」は後の書き入れである。それでも堺と国友を押さえた織田と、甲斐の武田の差ははっきりしていた。

世が豊臣のものになると、鉄砲はどの家にも行きわたる。朝鮮への出兵で島津家に課された軍役は、鉄砲千五百、弓千五百、槍三百であった。遅れていた奥羽も追いつく。1615年の大坂夏の陣で、[[p:伊達政宗]]は一万ほどの軍に三千四百二十挺の鉄砲を持たせていた。
body.en:
In 1543 Portuguese aboard a ship driven ashore on Tanegashima carried iron tubes fired with a slow match. The lord of the island, Tanegashima Tokitaka, bought two and had his swordsmiths copy them. The craft passed to Negoro in Kii, Sakai in Izumi and Kunitomo in Ōmi. From there to the battlefield took, from house to house, anything up to twenty years more.

The west and the home provinces were early. The oldest record of guns used in battle is put in 1549, when [[p:島津貴久|Shimazu Takahisa]] of Satsuma attacked Kajiki in Ōsumi. In 1550 a courtier's diary notes a man of the Miyoshi side killed by a gunshot in the eastern hills of Kyoto. In 1553, when [[p:織田信長|Oda Nobunaga]] went to meet his father-in-law Saitō Dōsan, five hundred bows and guns were carried in his train.

They reached the east too. In 1555 [[p:武田信玄|Takeda Shingen]] sent eight hundred bows and three hundred guns into Asahiyama castle in Shinano. Nagao Kagetora, the later [[p:上杉謙信|Uesugi Kenshin]], going up to Kyoto in 1559, was given by the shogun [[p:足利義輝|Ashikaga Yoshiteru]] a paper on how to mix gunpowder.

But the numbers differed. Set the surviving muster rolls side by side: the Uesugi in 1575 owe 316 guns among something over 5,500 men, about one in seventeen; the Hōjō men of Iwatsuki in 1577, fifty-odd among 1,580, one in thirty. The Chōsokabe of Tosa, by their own retainer's admission, had old gear and few guns beside the armies of Toyotomi.

What made the difference was shot and powder. Saltpetre, which powder needs, was hardly to be found in Japan and came by ship from Ming China and south-east Asia, through Sakai and the ports of Kyushu. In 1567 [[p:大友宗麟|Ōtomo Sōrin]] wrote to the bishop at Macao asking that good saltpetre be sold each year to him alone, and none to his enemy the Mōri. Takeda Shingen ordered his vassals to bring guns "even if you cut down on long spears"; but Kai is far from the sea, and shot and powder were always short.

At Nagashino in 1575 the guns Oda Nobunaga placed behind the palisades under five commissioners were "about a thousand", says the Chronicle of Nobunaga; the famous "three thousand" is a later hand's addition. Even so the gap between the Oda, who held Sakai and Kunitomo, and the Takeda of Kai was plain.

Once the country was Toyotomi's, every house had guns. For the Korean expedition the Shimazu were assessed at fifteen hundred guns, fifteen hundred bows and three hundred spears. The north, long behind, caught up: at the summer siege of Osaka in 1615 [[p:伊達政宗|Date Masamune]] had 3,420 guns in an army of about ten thousand.

legend:上杉家軍役帳・北条家着到定|the Uesugi and Hōjō muster rolls

body.ja:
車懸かり (くるまがかり) は、[[p:上杉謙信]]が川中島で用いたと伝えられる攻め方である。出どころは武田方の軍記『甲陽軍鑑』で、上杉方の確かな記録には見えない。

1561年九月十日の朝、信濃の八幡原。霧が晴れると、妻女山にいるはずの上杉軍が[[p:武田信玄]]の本隊の目の前にいた。信玄は物見に上杉の陣立てを尋ねた。『甲陽軍鑑』はその答えをこう書く。「謙信の陣は車懸かりといって、幾回り目かに旗本と敵の旗本とを打ち合わせて一戦をする備えである。」

後の人々は、これを車輪が回るように隊が次々に入れ替わって攻めかかる陣形だと説いた。先頭の隊が戦っては脇へ退き、次の隊が新手として当たる。輪が回るうちに、謙信の旗本が信玄の旗本に行き当たる。攻められる側は休む間がなく、どこを突けば崩れるのかも分からない。

今の研究者の多くは、輪になって回る陣形が本当に組めたとは考えていない。夜のうちに山を下りて川を渡った上杉軍は、行軍の列のまま霧の中で武田の本隊に行き当たり、着いた隊から順に戦いに加わった。それが武田の側からは、新手が次々に湧いて出る車輪のように見えた、という説明がよく行われる。

この日、武田方は信玄の弟の信繁と、軍師とされる[[p:山本勘助]]を失った。『甲陽軍鑑』は、白い布で頭を包んだ武者がただ一騎で信玄の床几に乗りつけ、三太刀斬りつけ、信玄は立ち上がる間もなく軍配で受けたと語る。軍配にはあとで見ると八つの傷があったという。上杉方の記録は、斬りつけたのは荒川伊豆守という家臣だとする。

上杉の兵の中身は、1575年の軍役の帳面から分かる。槍が三分の二、馬上は十人に一人、鉄砲は十七人に一人。変わった兵がいたわけではない。車懸かりが実在したとすれば、それは兵の種類ではなく、謙信がその兵をどう動かしたかの話である。
body.en:
The kurumagakari, the "wheel attack", is how [[p:上杉謙信|Uesugi Kenshin]] is said to have fought at Kawanakajima. The source is the Kōyō gunkan, a war chronicle of the Takeda side; no sure record of the Uesugi mentions it.

On the morning of the tenth of the ninth month, 1561, at Hachimanbara in Shinano, the mist lifted and the Uesugi army — supposed to be up on Saijo hill — stood right in front of [[p:武田信玄|Takeda Shingen]]'s main body. Shingen asked his scouts how the Uesugi were drawn up. The Kōyō gunkan gives the answer: "Kenshin's array is what is called kurumagakari: an order in which, at some turn of the wheel, his headquarters meets the enemy's headquarters and fights it."

Later ages explained it as a formation in which units took turns like the spokes of a turning wheel: the leading unit fought and drew off to the side, the next came on fresh, and as the wheel went round Kenshin's own guard came up against Shingen's. The side attacked had no rest and could not tell where to strike to break it.

Most scholars today doubt that anyone could really have formed and turned such a wheel. The usual account is that the Uesugi, having come down the hill and across the river in the night, ran into the Takeda main body in the mist still in column of march, and each unit joined the fight as it arrived — which, from the Takeda side, looked like a wheel bringing up fresh men without end.

That day the Takeda lost Shingen's brother Nobushige and [[p:山本勘助|Yamamoto Kansuke]], held to be his strategist. The Kōyō gunkan tells of a warrior with his head wrapped in white cloth riding alone up to Shingen's camp stool and cutting at him three times, while Shingen, with no time to rise, parried with his war fan; the fan, looked at afterwards, bore eight cuts. The Uesugi record says the rider was a retainer, Arakawa Izu-no-kami.

What the Uesugi army was made of is known from the muster roll of 1575: two men in three with spears, one in ten mounted, one in seventeen with a gun. There was no strange kind of soldier in it. If the wheel attack was real, it was not a kind of troops but a matter of how Kenshin moved the troops he had.

src: legend:上杉家御年譜|the Uesugi house annals

title.en: The five colours of the Hōjō

body.ja:
[[p:北条氏康]]の時代、小田原の北条家には、旗と具足の色で分けた五つの軍団があったと伝えられる。黄・赤・青・白・黒の「五色備え (ごしきぞなえ)」である。後の軍記や江戸時代の書物に見える話で、同じ時代の文書で五つがそろって確かめられるわけではない。

伝えによれば、黄備えは[[p:北条綱成]]、赤備えは北条綱高、青備えは富永直勝、白備えは笠原康勝、黒備えは多目元忠が率いた。いずれも氏康を支えた重臣である。色で備えを分けるのは、広い戦場でどの隊がどこにいるかを大将が一目で見分けるための工夫であった。武田や井伊の赤備えと同じ考えである。

このうち確かな物が残るのは黄備えである。北条綱成は、朽葉色 (黄) の絹に「八幡」と大きく書いた旗を掲げた。人はこれを「地黄八幡 (じきはちまん)」と呼んだ。綱成は戦のたびに先頭に立ち、「勝った、勝った」と叫びながら斬り込んだという。

1546年の河越の夜戦で、綱成は半年のあいだ三千の兵で河越城を守り抜いた。囲んでいたのは、関東管領の上杉と古河公方の連合軍、八万ともいう。氏康は八千を率いて救いに来ると、偽って降参を申し出て敵を油断させ、夜、兵に鎧を脱がせて白い布を目印に付けさせ、敵の陣に斬り込んだ。城の中からも綱成が打って出た。扇谷上杉家はこの夜に滅び、北条は関東の主となった。黒備えの多目元忠は、深追いする氏康を見て法螺貝を吹かせ、兵を引かせたと伝わる。

青備えの富永直勝は1564年、国府台で里見と戦って討死した。

地黄八幡の旗は今も残っている。1571年、駿河の深沢城を守っていた綱成は、[[p:武田信玄]]に金掘り衆で城を掘り崩されて開城した。このとき城に残された旗を、信玄は「左衛門大夫 (綱成) の武勇にあやかれ」と言って、[[p:真田幸隆]]の子の源次郎 (信昌) に与えた。旗は真田家に伝わり、信州の松代に現存する。
body.en:
In [[p:北条氏康|Hōjō Ujiyasu]]'s day the Hōjō of Odawara are said to have had five corps told apart by the colour of their banners and armour: yellow, red, blue, white and black — the goshiki-zonae, the "five-colour array". The story comes from later war tales and books of the Edo period; documents of the time do not confirm all five together.

By the tradition the yellow was led by [[p:北条綱成|Hōjō Tsunashige]], the red by Hōjō Tsunataka, the blue by Tominaga Naokatsu, the white by Kasahara Yasukatsu and the black by Tame Mototada, all great retainers of Ujiyasu. Dividing corps by colour let a commander see at a glance, on a wide field, which body was where — the same thought as the red troops of the Takeda and the Ii.

The one with firm evidence is the yellow. Hōjō Tsunashige flew a banner of russet-yellow silk with the name of the war god Hachiman written large on it; men called it the Jiki Hachiman, the "yellow-ground Hachiman". He was always at the front, it is said, charging in with the shout "We've won! We've won!"

In the night battle of Kawagoe in 1546 Tsunashige had held Kawagoe castle for half a year with three thousand men against the allied armies of the Uesugi deputy and the Koga lord — eighty thousand, by some accounts. Ujiyasu came to its relief with eight thousand, lulled the enemy with a false offer to surrender, and by night had his men leave off their armour, wear white cloth as a sign, and fall on the enemy camp; Tsunashige sallied from the castle at the same time. The Ōgigayatsu Uesugi were destroyed that night, and the Hōjō were masters of the Kantō. Tame Mototada of the black corps, seeing Ujiyasu pursue too far, is said to have had the conch blown to call the men back.

Tominaga Naokatsu of the blue corps fell fighting the Satomi at Kōnodai in 1564.

The Jiki Hachiman banner still exists. In 1571 Tsunashige, holding Fukasawa castle in Suruga, gave it up when [[p:武田信玄|Takeda Shingen]]'s miners dug the place out from under him. The banner was left behind, and Shingen gave it to Genjirō, a son of [[p:真田幸隆|Sanada Yukitaka]], telling him to take after the valour of the man who had flown it. It came down in the Sanada house and is kept at [[p:まつ|Matsu]]shiro in Shinano.

src: legend:地黄八幡旗指物 (真田宝物館)|the Jiki Hachiman banner (Sanada treasures, Matsushiro)

ties.ja: 草履取りから仕えた秀吉を、信長は「猿」「禿げ鼠」と呼んで可愛がり、重く用いた。
ties.en: Nobunaga called Hideyoshi, who began as his sandal-bearer, "monkey" and "bald rat", and raised him high.

ties.ja: 信長の弟信勝に従って背いた勝家は、許されてからは織田家の筆頭の将となった。
ties.en: Katsuie once rebelled with Nobunaga's brother; pardoned, he became the first of Oda's generals.

ties.ja: 1582年、光秀は本能寺の信長を襲った。理由は今も謎である。
ties.en: In 1582 Mitsuhide fell on Nobunaga at Honnōji — why is still a mystery.

ties.ja: 利家は若い頃「槍の又左」と呼ばれた信長の側近であった。
ties.en: In his youth Toshiie was one of Nobunaga's pages, "Mataza of the spear".

ties.ja: 牛一は信長の一代記『信長公記』を書き残した。
ties.en: [[p:太田牛一|Ōta Gyūichi]] wrote Nobunaga's chronicle.

ties.ja: 永徳は安土城の障壁画を描いた。
ties.en: Eitoku painted the walls of Azuchi castle.

ties.ja: 信長はフロイスと十数回も会い、遠い国々の話を好んで聞いた。
ties.en: Nobunaga met Frois more than a dozen times, eager to hear of faraway lands.

ties.ja: 信長の妹[[p:お市]]を妻に迎えながら、長政は朝倉との古い盟約を選び、金ヶ崎で信長を挟み撃ちにしかけた。
ties.en: Married to Nobunaga's sister [[p:お市|Oichi]], Nagamasa chose his old alliance with the Asakura and nearly trapped Nobunaga at Kanegasaki.

ties.ja: 久秀は二度にわたって信長に背き、最後は信貴山城で滅んだ。
ties.en: Hisahide rebelled against Nobunaga twice, and perished at last at Shigisan.

ties.ja: 有岡城で信長に背いた村重は、説得に来た[[p:黒田官兵衛]]を一年も土牢に閉じ込めた。
ties.en: Rebelling at Arioka, Murashige threw [[p:黒田官兵衛|Kuroda Kanbei]], who came to talk him round, into a dungeon for a year.

ties.ja: 官兵衛が裏切ったと思い込んだ信長に、官兵衛の子を殺せと命じられた半兵衛は、ひそかに子をかくまって救った。
ties.en: Ordered by Nobunaga, who thought Kanbei a traitor, to kill Kanbei's son, Hanbei hid the boy and saved him.

ties.ja: 秀吉は官兵衛の才を恐れ、「わしの後に天下を取るのはあの男だ」と言ったという。
ties.en: Hideyoshi feared Kanbei's gifts: "the one who will take the realm after me is that man," he is said to have remarked.

ties.ja: 「三献の茶」。寺の小僧だった三成は、喉の渇いた秀吉にぬるい茶をたっぷり、次に少し熱く、最後に熱い茶を少しだけ出し、その気配りで召し抱えられたという。
ties.en: "Three cups of tea." As a temple boy, Mitsunari served the thirsty Hideyoshi a big cup of lukewarm tea, then a smaller, hotter one, then a little very hot — and was taken into his service for his thoughtfulness, the story goes.

ties.ja: 賤ヶ岳で手柄を立てた「七本槍」の一人。
ties.en: One of the "Seven Spears" of Shizugatake.

ties.ja: 七本槍の筆頭。
ties.en: First of the Seven Spears.

ties.ja: 茶頭として重んじた利休に、秀吉は1591年、切腹を命じた。
ties.en: In 1591 Hideyoshi ordered Rikyū, his honoured tea master, to take his own life.

ties.ja: 弟の秀長は秀吉を陰で支え、秀長が死ぬと豊臣家に影がさした。
ties.en: His brother Hidenaga was his steady support; when Hidenaga died a shadow fell over the house.

ties.ja: 茶会で、病の吉継の膿が茶碗に落ち、皆が飲むのをためらった。三成は平然と飲み干したという。吉継は負けると知りながら三成のために関ヶ原で戦った。
ties.en: At a tea gathering pus from the sick Yoshitsugu's face fell into the shared bowl and no one would drink; Mitsunari drank it off, the story goes. Yoshitsugu fought for him at Sekigahara knowing they would lose.

ties.ja: 朝鮮の陣以来、武断派の清正・正則らと三成は激しく対立した。
ties.en: From the Korean campaigns the fighting generals Kiyomasa and Masanori loathed Mitsunari.

ties.ja: 関ヶ原の昼過ぎ、松尾山の秀秋は東軍に寝返った。
ties.en: Past noon at Sekigahara, Hideaki on Mount [[p:まつ|Matsu]]o went over to the east.

ties.ja: 五十余度の戦で傷一つ負わなかったという猛将。「家康に過ぎたるもの」とうたわれた。
ties.en: A fierce warrior said never to have been wounded in fifty-odd battles — "more than Ieyasu deserves", people sang.

ties.ja: 本能寺の変の後、半蔵は家康を伊賀の山越えで三河へ逃がした。
ties.en: After Honnōji Hanzō led Ieyasu to safety over the hills of Iga.

ties.ja: 家康は正信を「友」と呼び、二人きりで長く語り合ったという。
ties.en: Ieyasu called Masanobu his "friend", and talked with him alone for hours.

ties.ja: 1585年、家康の重臣数正は突然秀吉のもとへ走った。
ties.en: In 1585 Kazumasa, one of Ieyasu's chief retainers, suddenly went over to Hideyoshi.

ties.ja: 五度の川中島。信玄が死んだと聞いた謙信は、食事の箸を落として泣いたという。
ties.en: Five battles at Kawanakajima. Hearing Shingen was dead, Kenshin dropped his chopsticks and wept, they say.

ties.ja: 無口な景勝と才気の兼続は、生涯の主従であった。
ties.en: Silent Kagekatsu and brilliant Kanetsugu were lord and retainer for life.

ties.ja: 幼い政宗の、病で飛び出した右目を、景綱が小刀で切り取ったという話が伝わる。
ties.en: The story goes that Kagetsuna cut out with a knife the young Masamune's eye, which disease had made bulge.

ties.ja: 大友家の二つの柱。道雪は紹運の子宗茂を婿養子に迎えた。
ties.en: The two pillars of the Ōtomo; Dōsetsu adopted Jōun's son Muneshige as his heir.

ties.ja: 「願わくば我に七難八苦を与えたまえ」。尼子家の再興に生涯をかけた。
ties.en: "Grant me seven troubles and eight sorrows." He gave his life to restoring the Amago.

ties.ja: 天下一の絵師の座を争った二人。
ties.en: Rivals for the title of first painter of the realm.

ties.ja: 1612年、巌流島で二人は決闘し、遅れて来た武蔵が櫂を削った木刀で小次郎を倒したと伝わる。
ties.en: In 1612 they duelled on Ganryūjima; Musashi, arriving late, struck Kojirō down with a sword carved from an oar, so the story goes.

ties.ja: 大坂の陣で豊臣方の牢人衆を率いた二人。又兵衛は道明寺で討死した。
ties.en: The two led the masterless warriors on the Toyotomi side at Osaka; Matabei died at Dōmyōji.

ties.ja: 氏郷は右近に導かれてキリスト教に親しんだ。
ties.en: Ujisato came to Christianity through Ukon.

ties.ja: 人質だった少年氏郷の才を見抜いた信長は、娘を嫁がせた。
ties.en: Seeing the gifts of the boy hostage, Nobunaga gave him his daughter in marriage.

ties.ja: 光秀の娘玉 (ガラシャ) は藤孝の子忠興の妻。だが本能寺の後、藤孝は髪を下ろして光秀に味方しなかった。
ties.en: Mitsuhide's daughter Tama (Gracia) was married to Fujitaka's son; yet after Honnōji Fujitaka shaved his head and would not join Mitsuhide.

marriages.ja: 美濃の斎藤道三の娘帰蝶 ([[p:濃姫]])。尾張と美濃の和を結ぶ政略の結婚であった。道三は娘に短刀を持たせ、「信長がうつけなら刺せ」と言うと、娘は「この刀は父上を刺すことになるかもしれません」と答えた、という話が伝わる。
marriages.en: Kichō ([[p:濃姫|Lady Nō]]), daughter of Saitō Dōsan of Mino: a political match sealing peace between Owari and Mino. Dōsan, the story goes, gave her a dagger to kill Nobunaga if he proved a fool; she answered that it might be her father she used it on.

marriages.ja: 身分の違いを越えた、当時には珍しい恋愛による結婚とも言われる。[[p:ねね]]はのちに北政所と呼ばれ、秀吉の天下を内から支えた。信長はねねに、秀吉の浮気を戒める手紙を送り「あの禿げ鼠にはそなた以上の妻は見つからぬ」と書いている。
marriages.en: A love match across ranks, rare in that age, it is said. [[p:ねね|Nene]], later called Kita-no-Mandokoro, upheld Hideyoshi's rule from within. Nobunaga wrote her a letter about Hideyoshi's philandering: "that bald rat will never find a better wife than you."

marriages.ja: 信長の妹[[p:お市]]は、北近江の[[p:浅井長政]]に嫁いだ。織田と浅井の同盟の証であった。長政が信長に背き、小谷城が落ちたとき、お市は三人の娘 (茶々・初・江) とともに織田の陣へ送り返された。
marriages.en: Nobunaga's sister [[p:お市|Oichi]] married [[p:浅井長政|Azai Nagamasa]] of northern Ōmi, the pledge of the Oda–Azai alliance. When Nagamasa turned on Nobunaga and Odani fell, Oichi and her three daughters — Chacha, Hatsu and Gō — were sent back to the Oda camp.

marriages.ja: 本能寺の後、清洲会議を経て[[p:お市]]は[[p:柴田勝家]]に再嫁した。翌年、賤ヶ岳で勝家が秀吉に敗れると、二人は北ノ庄城で共に自害した。娘たちは城から逃された。
marriages.en: After Honnōji and the Kiyosu council, [[p:お市|Oichi]] remarried [[p:柴田勝家|Shibata Katsuie]]. The next year Katsuie was beaten by Hideyoshi at Shizugatake, and the two killed themselves together at Kitanoshō; the daughters were sent out of the castle.

marriages.ja: [[p:お市]]の長女茶々は、かつて母を死に追いやった秀吉の側室となった。淀城を与えられて[[p:淀殿]]と呼ばれ、秀頼を生んだ。
marriages.en: [[p:お市|Oichi]]'s eldest daughter Chacha became the concubine of Hideyoshi, the man who had driven her mother to her death. Given Yodo castle, she was called [[p:淀殿|Lady Yodo]], and bore Hideyori.

marriages.ja: [[p:今川義元]]の姪を母に持つ[[p:築山殿]]は、今川家の人質だった若い家康の妻となった。1579年、武田に通じたと疑われ、子の信康とともに死を命じられた。
marriages.en: [[p:築山殿|Lady Tsukiyama]], whose mother was a niece of [[p:今川義元|Imagawa Yoshimoto]], married the young Ieyasu while he was an Imagawa hostage. In 1579, suspected of dealings with the Takeda, she was put to death, and her son Nobuyasu ordered to kill himself.

marriages.ja: [[p:まつ]]は十二歳で利家に嫁いだ。のちに利家が秀吉と[[p:柴田勝家]]の間で迷ったとき、秀吉との間を取り持ったのはまつであった。関ヶ原の前には自ら江戸へ人質に下り、前田家を守った。
marriages.en: [[p:まつ|Matsu]] married Toshiie at twelve. When Toshiie wavered between Hideyoshi and [[p:柴田勝家|Shibata Katsuie]], it was she who made his peace with Hideyoshi; before Sekigahara she went to Edo herself as a hostage to keep the Maeda safe.

marriages.ja: [[p:お市]]の三女江は、三度目の結婚で家康の子秀忠に嫁ぎ、三代将軍家光を生んだ。姉の[[p:淀殿]]は大坂城で徳川と戦い、妹の江は徳川の妻として生きた。
marriages.en: [[p:お市|Oichi]]'s third daughter Gō, on her third marriage, wed Ieyasu's son Hidetada and bore the third shogun, Iemitsu. Her elder sister [[p:淀殿|Lady Yodo]] fought the Tokugawa at Osaka; Gō lived as a Tokugawa wife.

marriages.ja: 家康の孫[[p:千姫]]は、七歳で秀頼に嫁いだ。秀吉との約束を果たす政略の結婚であった。大坂夏の陣で、千姫は燃える城から救い出された。
marriages.en: Ieyasu's granddaughter Sen married Hideyori at seven, keeping a promise made to Hideyoshi. In the summer siege of Osaka she was rescued from the burning castle.

marriages.ja: 田村家の娘[[p:愛姫]]は、十二歳で政宗に嫁いだ。田村家との同盟が伊達の南奥州での足場となった。
marriages.en: Megohime of the Tamura married Masamune at twelve; the Tamura alliance was the Date foothold in southern Ōu.
